item.title: Canton of Solothurn: inheritance and gift tax
item.description: Swiss taxation at three levels: for the Canton of Solothurn, kinship, exemptions, declaration and deadlines matter.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Swiss tax system has three levels. - Each Canton has its own law and multiplier. - The municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax. - Kinship, exemptions and deadlines guide the review.
## Key facts - Topic → inheritance and gift tax in the Canton of Solothurn - Tax rates → degree of kinship - Exemptions → spouse and descendants - Compliance requirements → declaration and deadlines - Levels → federal, cantonal and municipal - AFC/ESTV → direct federal tax and VAT - Cantonal administrations → cantonal and municipal taxation
Three tax levels define the Swiss framework: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. To understand inheritance and gift tax in the Canton of Solothurn, this distinction comes before comparing rates. Each Canton has its own law and multiplier; for municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. A rule relating to Solothurn should therefore not be treated as a national rule.
### The framework not to conflate The topic indicated by the source focuses on four elements: tax rates by degree of kinship, exemptions for spouses and descendants, declaration and deadlines to be observed. These are the fields to keep separate when analyzing an inheritance or gift. The family relationship guides the search for the applicable rate; being a spouse or descendant guides the verification of the exemption. The declaration component completes the check and requires following the deadline set by the applicable procedure.
The territorial factor and the family factor do not serve the same function: the former establishes the cantonal and municipal framework; the latter structures the search for the rate and exemption. The declaration connects the two levels and brings the review to the operational level.
| Level | Indicated reference | Jurisdiction | |---|---|---| | Federal | Direct federal tax and VAT | AFC/ESTV | | Cantonal | Cantonal taxation | Cantonal administrations | | Municipal | Municipal taxation and multiplier applied to the cantonal tax | Cantonal administrations |
The jurisdiction map helps avoid contacting the wrong office. AFC/ESTV handles direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxation. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, namely AVS/AI/LPP, but does not set taxes; UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. To organize the declaration component, the process can be supported by dichiarazione delle imposte, while keeping cantonal jurisdiction distinct.
The analysis therefore starts with the tax domicile, moves through the family relationship and reaches the compliance requirements. The Canton of Solothurn is the jurisdiction to examine; the three levels and the map of offices are the filter for avoiding confusion among rules, multipliers and responsibilities. ## From the framework to the practical decision
The concrete implication of the cantonal model is that the name of the tax alone is not enough to interpret the result. In a hypothetical scenario, whoever has to assess an inheritance or a gift starts with the transaction and the degree of kinship. Only afterward do they check whether the recipient falls into the category of spouse or descendants, because the editorial perspective requires a specific review of the relevant exemptions. The declaration and deadline are part of the same sequence, not a separate step.
### Three filters to avoid incorrect calculations The first filter is family-related. The tax rate must be sought in relation to the degree of kinship indicated by the Solothurn rule; the exemption must be verified for the categories mentioned, spouse and descendants. The second filter is territorial. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier: a result referring to Solothurn cannot automatically be transferred to another canton. The municipal framework must then remain visible, because the municipality's multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax.
| Filter | Practical question | |---|---| | Transaction | Is it an inheritance or a gift? | | Kinship | What is the relevant degree? | | Exemption | Does the spouse or descendant category apply? | | Procedure | Which declaration and which deadline must be observed? |
The third filter is institutional. AFC/ESTV concerns direct federal tax and VAT, while cantonal and municipal taxation falls within the cantonal administrations. UFAS/BSV is linked to AVS, AI and LPP, not to setting taxes; UST/BFS produces statistics, not tax rates. This separation prevents using a social-security or statistical reference to resolve a tax issue.
For a concrete comparison, the sheet should show the transaction, family relationship, any exemption, tax level and deadline separately. If one item remains mixed in with the others, it becomes difficult to understand whether one is reading a cantonal rule, a municipal step or a federal competence.
A calcolatore stipendio/imposte can help organize a general numerical check, but the interpretation must remain anchored in the law of the canton and the parameters of the case. The practical advantage is having a sheet in which kinship, exemption, tax level and deadline remain legible without overlapping different areas of responsibility.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to organize the verification
The concrete action consists of turning the topic into a short, traceable sequence. The worksheet must start from the tax situation of the Canton of Solothurn and keep the cantonal level, the municipal level and any federal reference separate. This way, the search for tax rates is not mixed with the verification of exemptions or with the deadline for the return.
### Five operational steps 1. Classify the transaction. Indicate whether the case concerns an inheritance or a gift. 2. Define the kinship. State the relevant degree of kinship and separately verify the status of a spouse or descendant. 3. Set the territorial scope. Use the law of the Canton of Solothurn and consider the municipality without confusing its multiplier with the cantonal one. 4. Choose the correct point of contact. For direct federal tax and VAT, the point of reference is AFC/ESTV; for cantonal and municipal taxation, the cantonal administrations are responsible. 5. Complete the procedural part. Include the return and the deadline to be observed in the same verification of the tax rate and any exemption.
The sequence also serves to rule out two shortcuts. The first is to look for a single answer for all Cantons, when the source establishes that each Canton has its own law and multiplier. The second is to ask an entity that performs another function for a tax rate: UFAS/BSV concerns AVS, AI and LPP, while UST/BFS deals with statistics and does not set taxes.
The criterion also applies to communication between levels: a request concerning cantonal or municipal taxation must be kept separate from a request concerning direct federal tax and VAT. Separating the functions makes the case file more readable and makes it possible to check that kinship, exemption and deadline have been addressed within the same Solothurn framework.
For the return-filing step, dichiarazione delle imposte can be used as an organizational aid, precisely stating the tax level and the applicable deadline. The final check must leave four items visible: transaction, kinship, territorial jurisdiction and procedure. item.title: Parliament: short sleep during session, power naps proposed
item.description: 16 parliamentarians sleep 6h10min during sessions (-50min). Rasch (University of Fribourg) proposes power-nap rooms at the Federal Palace.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 16 members of the National Council and Council of States slept 6 hours and 10 minutes - During sessions, about 50 minutes less than usual - Björn Rasch proposes spaces for power naps at the Federal Palace - Alcohol and sleeping pills affect the quality of rest
## Key facts - Who → members of the National Council and Council of States - Sample → 16 MPs and senators - Average → six hours and ten minutes per night - Difference → about 50 minutes less than usual - Proposed location → Federal Palace - Researcher → Björn Rasch, University of Fribourg - Objective → maintaining politicians' efficiency
Six hours and ten minutes of sleep per night: this is the average recorded during sessions by members of the National Council and Council of States. The figure, about 50 minutes below the usual duration, emerges from a study conducted at the University of Fribourg on 16 MPs and senators. Björn Rasch, 51, a sleep researcher and professor at the University of Fribourg, is the professional cited in the study. Blick reported on the study today.
### The figure and the proposal
For Rasch, tiredness is not a secondary detail. Tired people, he explains, tend to make riskier decisions than those who are rested. Those who sleep less, he adds, also have more difficulty assimilating information. In a Parliament called upon to discuss and make decisions during sessions, the connection between sleep and performance therefore becomes the focus of his proposal.
The scholar calls for spaces at the Federal Palace for short naps during the day. The so-called power naps, according to Rasch, actually increase performance capacity. The solution, in his words, is not to leave parliamentarians sitting in the chamber, awake but tired: «If a parliamentarian fell asleep in the chamber, it would immediately be a scandal; leaving them sitting, awake but tired, is not a solution: why not create spaces for recovery?». A rest room would, in his view, be a pragmatic approach to maintaining politicians' efficiency.
### Alcohol, sleeping pills and health
The quality of rest is also linked to alcoholic drinks often present at aperitifs on the sidelines of sessions. Alcohol can help one fall asleep, but in the second half of the night one wakes more often and remains awake longer. Sleeping pills help one fall asleep, without guaranteeing restorative rest; the study shows that only a minority of parliamentarians use them, in line with the general population.
Rasch argues that sleep should have greater priority in the national health strategy. From sleep disorders, he says, one can understand how stressed a person is; if they appear, the risk of burnout after two years increases. The researcher finally points to children and adolescents: when it comes to sleep, he concludes, more should be said at school. For the overall health picture, the reader can pair this news with the guide LAMal/cassa malati from Frontaliere Ticino. The national significance of the news is not presented as a new rule for workers, but as an issue related to the quality of decisions made during federal sessions. The source explicitly links fatigue to riskier decisions and a reduced ability to absorb information. For this reason, Rasch's proposal concerns the organization of the Federal Palace and, more generally, the national health strategy.
### What can be gleaned from the data
The sample consists of 16 deputies and senators. The text does not present it as a snapshot of the entire population and does not offer separate results for groups, sessions, or contexts. The only comparison indicated is with the usual sleep duration of those same parliamentarians: about 50 minutes more than the six hours and ten minutes recorded during the sessions.
The distinction matters because the proposal does not present the nap as a convenience, but rather as a tool to support performance. At the same time, the source does not indicate an already implemented project, costs, a timetable, or an authority tasked with creating the room. The data therefore fuels an organizational debate; it does not describe an adopted measure.
| Observed element | Possible interpretation according to the source | |---|---| | Sleep duration | Fatigue can affect decisions and the assimilation of information | | Power nap | A short rest increases performance capacity | | Alcohol | Falling asleep does not amount to quality rest | | Health strategy | Sleep should be given greater priority |
The passage on alcohol and sleeping pills also broadens the analysis: what matters is not only the time spent in bed, but also how the second half of the night unfolds and whether the rest is restorative. The source specifies that only a minority of parliamentarians use sleeping pills, in line with the general population; however, it does not offer any other figures.
The political follow-up indicated by Rasch is twofold: intervene earlier when sleep disorders signal stress and bring the issue into schools for children and adolescents. These are directions for action, not an already defined program. To read about this topic alongside the other daily dossiers, the site also offers the guide on costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. To turn the news into an actionable outline, the reader can follow four steps. These are reading and discussion steps, because the source does not indicate an administrative procedure, a deadline, or an obligation to follow.
### Four steps for reading the proposal
1. Separate the finding from the proposal. The first element is the survey of parliamentarians during sessions, with a shorter-than-usual sleep duration. The second is the idea of providing spaces for short naps at the Federal Palace. Treating the room as a proposal by Björn Rasch avoids presenting it as a decision that has already been adopted.
2. Look at quality, not just duration. The source mentions aperitifs with alcoholic beverages and explains that alcohol can make it easier to fall asleep, but can also lead to more frequent awakenings in the second half of the night. The same text specifies that sleeping pills help one fall asleep, without ensuring restorative rest. These are the two elements to keep distinct when assessing the issue.
3. Consider sleep as a possible sign of stress. Rasch argues that sleep disorders can reveal how much pressure a person is under and that, in such cases, it would be useful to intervene early. The source also links the disorders to an increased risk of burnout after two years, without indicating a specific path or an authority to turn to.
4. Extend the discussion to children and adolescents. The researcher concludes that sleep should be discussed more at school. Here too, the source indicates a direction, but does not describe an educational program, a deadline, or a concrete measure.
To follow the development of the issue, the point to observe is therefore the possible transition from the proposal for a room for rest to giving sleep greater priority in the national health strategy. item.title: Bern eases arms export restrictions
item.description: Popular vote on 29 novembre on the revision of the law on war materiel: more flexibility for exports and re-exports to 17 EU countries and other states
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Federal Council calls for a revision of the War Material Act - Popular vote on 29 November - Every export requires SECO authorization - The proposal concerns exports and re-exports
## Key facts - Subject → revision of the War Material Act - Date → 29 November - Control → SECO authorization for every export - European countries → 17 of the 27 EU member states - Other states mentioned → United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, New Zealand and Argentina - Stated objectives → defense capability and jobs
### The vote and the new scope
On 29 November, the Federal Council is calling for approval of the revision of the War Material Act, one of the items on the agenda of the next popular vote. The stated objective is to ensure the country's defense capability and safeguard jobs.
According to Keystone-ATS, it is currently forbidden to export Swiss war materiel to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. Since the beginning of the war waged by Russia against Ukraine, Bern believes that the Swiss arms industry has become unattractive because of the strict rules and is under heavy pressure.
On this basis, the bourgeois majority in Parliament wants to grant the Federal Council, under certain conditions, greater room for maneuver regarding exports and re-exports. The revision aims to facilitate the transfer by Western countries of material purchased in Switzerland to third countries, if compatible with Switzerland's neutrality and foreign and security policy interests.
The bill also provides for a Federal Council veto. In the presence of security or neutrality-policy concerns, the executive could require the weapons to remain in the purchasing country. In exceptional circumstances, and to protect foreign or security policy interests, it would be possible to deviate from the current authorization criteria, while respecting international obligations.
Another change is the abolition of the systematic requirement for purchasing states to request Swiss approval before transferring the material to another country. Seventeen European countries out of the 27 EU member states are listed, as well as the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, New Zealand and Argentina, among others, with export regimes similar to Switzerland's. Requests would be authorized in advance even in the event of armed conflict.
The referendum committee fears that the reform would make sales or transfers to authoritarian regimes or regimes that do not respect human rights possible, reducing Swiss control over re-exports. Guy Parmelin rejects this interpretation: every export would remain subject to SECO authorization and comply with neutrality law, human rights and other international obligations.
The DEFR presents the reform as a tool for ensuring greater flexibility in foreign policy during exceptional crises and strengthening the arms industry as the foundation of national defense. Simon Plüss, head of the Export Controls and Sanctions division at SECO, explained that the revision would make it possible to export to the United States components for the F-35s that Switzerland has decided to purchase, if they are not directly intended for combat use. ## What would change for the Swiss system
### The comparison between the current rule and the proposal
The practical difference is the leeway granted to the Federal Council, not the disappearance of controls. A veto would remain possible and every export would continue to require authorization from SECO. The novelty mainly concerns destinations, re-exports and exceptional crises.
| Area | Today | Proposed revision | |---|---|---| | Countries in conflict | Exports prohibited to countries involved in conflicts | Prior authorization for similar regimes, even if involved | | Re-exports | Swiss agreement systematically required | No longer systematic; veto and remaining in the purchasing country possible | | United States | No new authorization | F-35 components possible if not intended for combat | | Derogations | Current criteria apply | Possible in exceptional crises, in compliance with international obligations |
The first effect considered by Bern is industrial. Strict rules have made the Swiss arms industry unattractive and subject to pressure; greater flexibility is linked to national defense and jobs. For employment data, see aziende che assumono.
The case of the United States makes visible the difference between the current regime and the proposed one. Today, new authorizations are not possible because Swiss rules are stricter than the law of neutrality. The revision would instead open up the possibility of exporting components for the F-35, but subject to the limitation that their use not be directly intended for combat.
For the Western countries that have purchased materiel in Switzerland, the change would concern the next step: it would no longer be necessary to systematically request Swiss agreement for each transfer to a third country. However, the Federal Council's veto and the possibility of requiring that the weapons remain in the purchasing country would remain when concerns arise about security or neutrality.
The limits to flexibility would remain international obligations, the law of neutrality and respect for human rights. For this reason, the position of the referendum committee and that of the Federal Council describe two opposing assessments of the same mechanism: on the one hand, the fear of losing control over re-exports, on the other, the guarantee that SECO authorization would continue to apply to every export.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the dossier before 29 novembre
### Five verification steps
To read the proposal without confusing the rule currently in force with the possible one, it is advisable to follow a precise sequence.
1. Mark 29 novembre. The revision of the War Material Act is among the items in the popular vote indicated by the source. The date distinguishes the current framework from the political decision on the revision.
2. Start from the rule currently in force. Today, Swiss war material cannot be exported to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. This is the point of comparison for assessing every proposed change.
3. If you analyze a re-export, distinguish the transfer by a Western country to a third country from the final destination. Also check whether it is a state with an export regime similar to Switzerland's: the proposal mentions 17 European countries out of the 27 in the EU, as well as the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, New Zealand and Argentina.
4. Check the counterweights. Even with the revision, exports would remain subject to SECO authorization. The assessment should comply with the law of neutrality, human rights and Switzerland's other international obligations.
5. Isolate exceptional situations. The Federal Council could exercise a veto, require that the weapons remain in the purchasing country, or deviate from the current authorization criteria for foreign or security policy interests. In the case of the F-35, the stated condition is that the components not be directly intended for use in combat.
In the political comparison, keep the two positions expressed in the source separate: the referendum committee fears transfers to authoritarian regimes and a loss of control; the Federal Council denies that this is a blank check. Those following the dossier for work can supplement their reading with the annunci di lavoro. To delve deeper into the personal economic side, use the calcolatore stipendio.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/berna-vuole-allentare-le-restrizioni-sulle-esportazione-di-armi/92139782)*

item.title: Arms exports: law revision put to a vote
item.description: The Federal Council proposes relaxing the rules on exports of war materiel. Vote scheduled for 29 novembre.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The vote on the revision is scheduled for November 29. - Bern wants to relax the rules on exports. - Objectives: Swiss defense and jobs. - Authorizations and international obligations remain.
## Key facts - Subject→revision of the War Materiel Act - Authority→Federal Council - Date→November 29 - Location→Bern - Current rule→ban on exports to countries involved in conflicts - Voice→Guy Parmelin, President of the Confederation and head of DEFR
On September 29, 2026, from Bern, the Federal Council called for approval of the revision of the War Materiel Act on November 29. The stated objective is to relax export rules to ensure Switzerland's defense capability and safeguard jobs.
Today, Swiss war materiel may not be exported to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. According to Bern, since the beginning of the war waged by Russia against Ukraine, these strict rules have made the domestic arms industry unattractive and subjected it to strong pressure.
### What the revision provides
The amendment is one of the items on the agenda of the November 29 popular vote. The center-right majority in Parliament intends to grant the Federal Council, under certain conditions, greater room for maneuver regarding exports and re-exports. The operational objective is to facilitate the transfer to third countries, by Western countries, of war materiel purchased in Switzerland.
The reform would also grant the Federal Council a right of veto. The executive could require weapons to remain in the purchasing country when security or neutrality-policy concerns arise. In exceptional circumstances, to safeguard foreign-policy or security interests, it would be possible to depart from the current authorization criteria, while always respecting international obligations.
Guy Parmelin, President of the Confederation and head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research, rejected the idea of unrestricted approval: > «In no case is this a blank cheque for the Federal Council»
He reiterated that every export would remain subject to authorization and would have to comply with the law of neutrality, human rights and Switzerland's other international obligations.
For Bern, the dossier also concerns the possibility of obtaining war materiel in a crisis. Parmelin links this objective to remaining in international value-creation chains and to the industry's competitiveness. The position expressed by the Federal Council is that strengthening the sector serves the national security of a neutral country that is not part of any defense alliance. The reference to jobs remains one of the stated objectives. To understand the effect of the revision, the practical question is how much it changes the decision-making leeway without turning exports into an unrestricted act. The text presented by Berna describes a conditional opening: more room for the Federal Council, but authorizations, veto power and international obligations remain central.
### Before and after the vote
| Step | Rule or scenario indicated | |---|---| | Current rules | Exporting Swiss war materiel to countries involved in internal or international conflicts is prohibited. | | If approved | Greater leeway for exports and re-exports, under certain conditions. | | Reservations | Federal Council veto and the possible requirement to leave the weapons in the purchasing country. | | Exceptional circumstances | Exemption from the current criteria in the interests of foreign or security policy, while respecting international obligations. |
The distinction serves to avoid confusing the vote on the law with the individual authorizations. The subject of 29 novembre is the revision; even under the framework described for the future, every export of war materiel would remain subject to authorization. The change would therefore concern the Federal Council's ability to assess certain cases with greater flexibility, not the elimination of the authorization process.
The text links greater flexibility to the viability of the arms industry and the preservation of jobs. The objective is presented as strengthening the defense industrial base. To distinguish legislative reporting from research on employment, one can consult annunci di lavoro and aziende che assumono.
The procurement rationale adds a second layer. In the event of a crisis, according to Parmelin, arms industries respond first and foremost to the needs of their own country. Switzerland should therefore remain integrated into international value-creation chains in order to maintain a competitive industry. The argument concerns not only sales abroad: it links an industrial presence to the possibility of obtaining war materiel when Switzerland needs it.
The stated political constraints remain: neutrality, human rights, international obligations and the absence of defense alliances delimit the proposed flexibility. For Berna, the revision seeks to reconcile more manageable transfers, security and the country's neutral position.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. To follow the dossier before 29 novembre, it is advisable to separate three levels: the subject of the vote, the powers that the revision would grant the Federal Council, and the limits that would remain applicable. An orderly reading avoids treating the proposal as an authorization already in force.
### The five-step process
1. Set the deadline. 29 novembre is the date of the popular vote on the revision of the law on war materiel. The step indicated is therefore the vote on the legislative amendment. 2. Start from the current rule. The reference point is the prohibition on exporting Swiss war materiel to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. 3. Isolate the new powers. Read separately the greater leeway on exports and re-exports, the right of veto, and the possibility of requesting that the weapons remain in the purchasing country. 4. Check the exception. The derogation from the current criteria is linked to exceptional circumstances and the protection of foreign-policy or security interests. Compliance with international obligations remains required. 5. Compare the arguments. On the one hand, Bern indicates defense capabilities, jobs, supplies and international value-creation chains. On the other hand, the framework retains neutrality, human rights, authorizations and federal control.
This outline makes it possible to distinguish what would change from what would remain unchanged. The Federal Council is asking for greater leeway to address exceptional crises; the same approach reiterates that every export must go through an authorization. The proposal also links the revision to Switzerland's specific situation: neutrality and absence from any defense alliance.
For a practical assessment of the employment issue, the criterion indicated is the link between the competitiveness of the arms industry and integration into international chains. Those following the dossier can therefore use the vote on 29 novembre as a political reference and keep research on employment separate from the decision on the law. To assess income separately from the political dossier, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Samedan airport reneal
item.description: Following the yes vote of 17 August 2025 (>54% of those entitled to vote), the 68,5 million renovation of Samedan Airport remains blocked by the appeal to the Federal Supreme Court; investments planned for 2027 amount to 7,6 million, deadline 2031.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The 68,5-million construction project is still stalled - The vote of 17 agosto 2025 surpassed 54% - The appeal to the Federal Supreme Court is blocking the start of the works - Investments of 7,6 million are planned for 2027
## Key facts - Project → renovation of Samedan Airport - Cost → 68,5 million francs - Vote → 17 agosto 2025 - Outcome → more than 54% of those entitled to vote - Appeal → pending before the Federal Supreme Court - Investments 2027 → 7,6 million - Expected deadline → 2031 - Source → ATS (Keystone-ATS)
On 17 agosto 2025, more than 54% of eligible voters in the eleven municipalities of Upper Engadine approved the renovation of Samedan Airport. More than a year after the popular vote in favor, however, the 68,5-million-franc construction project has not yet begun. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS.
The airport, dating back to 1938, is in urgent need of renovation. The project includes two new operations centers with a hangar for aircraft, the expansion and repair of the aprons in front of the airport, a tower with a 360-degree view, and a security fence. The vote therefore gave political approval to the infrastructure, but so far has not led to the opening of the construction site.
### The appeal keeping the project stalled
The project is being blocked by an appeal seeking to annul the popular vote of 17 agosto 2025. The Federal Supreme Court has ruled on the suspensive effect, but not yet on the merits. The appellant had asked that, until the final decision, measures to implement the project be halted, especially detailed planning and authorization of the credits for the second stage. The start of the contested works therefore remains subject to the Federal Supreme Court's final decision.
At the meeting of the airport conference, the political decision-making body, Mario Cavigelli, president of Infra, which owns the infrastructure, described the condition of the airport in stark terms: > “We have to be honest: we are facing a ruin.” The structural problems that emerge are being dealt with discreetly, in the hope that the complete renovation can take place soon.
The fence follows a particular course. No objection was filed against its construction, but the start planned for the third quarter of this year will be delayed once again because of the appeal in Lausanne.
The supervisory complaint submitted in June by the Management Commission of the Municipality of S-chanf to the Grisons Government remains a separate matter. The request concerned a special investigation and an examination of Infra's accounting and reporting practices. On 10 agosto, the Cantonal Department of Finance and Municipalities had found no grounds for intervention. S-chanf requested a further review at the end of August, but the Canton maintained its position. ## What changes in practical terms
The practical point for anyone following the dossier is not to confuse three steps. The popular vote approved the project, the Federal Supreme Court is examining the appeal, and the airport conference still has to approve the budget items if the decision is favorable. These are different stages: the first expresses political consent, the second conditions implementation, and the third precedes the start indicated by Mario Cavigelli.
The distinction is also useful for reading updates without turning every announcement into a construction start date. Infra has prepared various decisions to proceed promptly with awarding the work to designers and contractors, but the source places the start after two steps: a favorable decision by the Federal Supreme Court and approval of the budget items by the conference. Administrative preparation therefore signals readiness, not the start of the work.
### Timelines, investments and budget
| Scenario or checkpoint | Effect indicated in the source | |---|---| | Favorable decision by the Federal Supreme Court | The conference must approve the budget items; afterward, work could begin | | Merits still pending | The start of the contested works remains subject to the final decision | | 2027 budget | Investments amounting to 7,6 million are planned | | Schedule | Completion in 2031 is described as extremely difficult and probably unrealistic |
The budget approved by the politicians, with only the Municipality of Samedan opposed, provides a precise financial reference. It should not, however, be confused with the total project cost, set at 68,5 million francs, or with a new authorization already sufficient to open the construction site. The airport conference brings together one representative from each of the eleven municipalities of Upper Engadine, and this is precisely the body responsible for the step indicated by Cavigelli after a favorable decision by the Federal Supreme Court.
The debt issue also requires separate consideration. Municipal representatives raised questions about alleged debts of Infra; Claudio Dietrich, however, clarified that in the 2025 annual accounts the surplus is an accounting figure and does not correspond to actual debts. According to his explanation, Infra is not indebted to anyone. For a reader comparing the figures, the difference between the accounting figure and actual debt is therefore the point not to overlook.
Finally, the appeal has an effect that goes beyond the contested works: the fence, too, will be delayed despite there being no objections. The airport project should not be confused with costo della vita in Svizzera, which is a separate tool for assessing personal expenses.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the dossier
To follow the project without assigning it a deadline that the source does not confirm, it is advisable to use a control sheet based on the steps already indicated. It is not a new administrative procedure, but a way to correctly read the updates from the airport conference, the Federal Tribunal, and the municipalities involved.
### Five operational checks
1. Vote basis: report the date of August 17, 2025, the outcome above 54%, and the involvement of the eleven municipalities of Upper Engadine. This identifies the consultation, but does not set the start date of the construction site.
2. Judicial status: distinguish the suspensive effect, on which the FT has already ruled, from the merits of the appeal, which is still pending. An update on the first point does not equal a final decision on the second.
3. Political step: after a favorable decision, verify the approval of the budget items by the airport conference. The source indicates this step before the start of works; the conference includes a representative for each of the eleven municipalities.
4. Numbers to keep separate: the project is worth 68.5 million francs, while for 2027 investments of 7.6 million are planned. The two amounts serve different purposes and should not be presented as if they indicated the same item.

item.title: Parliament needs a place to sleep: power nap
item.description: During sessions, Swiss parliamentarians sleep an average of 6 hours and 10 minutes, about 50 minutes less than usual, according to Björn Rasch's study of 16 members of Parliament.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Parliamentarians sleep 6 hours and 10 minutes per night - Rasch's study concerns 16 parliamentarians - The proposal is to create spaces for short naps - Fatigue can make decisions riskier
## Key facts - Sample → 16 members of the National Council and the Council of States - Sleep during sessions → 6 hours and 10 minutes per night - Difference → approximately 50 minutes less than usual - Proposal → spaces for short naps at the Federal Palace - Researcher → Björn Rasch, professor at the University of Fribourg - Reported effects → riskier decisions and difficulty assimilating information - Reference → Blick
Six hours and ten minutes of sleep per night is the average recorded among Swiss parliamentarians during sessions. The figure is at the center of a study conducted by Björn Rasch, a sleep researcher and professor at the University of Fribourg, involving 16 members of the National Council and the Council of States. The study, reported today by Blick, indicates approximately 50 minutes less rest than usual.
For Rasch, the reduction is not merely a number related to schedules. Tired people, the researcher argues, tend to make riskier decisions and have greater difficulty assimilating information. Hence the connection between quality of rest and parliamentary work: a session may take place with representatives present, but fatigue can affect how they assess information and choices.
### The proposal at the Federal Palace
The proposal is to create spaces at the Federal Palace for short naps during the day, the so-called power nap. Rasch does not suggest sleeping in the chamber as a solution. He explains it with a question:
> «If a parliamentarian fell asleep in the chamber, it would immediately be a scandal; leaving them sitting there, awake but tired, is not a solution: why not create spaces for recovery?»
In his view, a room dedicated to rest could help maintain the parliamentarians' efficiency. The idea therefore concerns a brief, organized recovery in the Parliament's spaces.
The researcher ultimately broadens the topic beyond parliamentary life. He hopes that sleep will receive greater attention in the national strategy for salute, because sleep disorders can indicate stress levels and be associated with a greater risk of burnout in subsequent years. He also calls for more space for the topic in schools, especially for children and adolescents. The source thus presents a specific proposal for the Federal Palace and, at the same time, a broader request for greater attention to sleep. ## What the proposal really measures
The practical value of the survey lies first and foremost in its scope. The data concerns 16 members of the National Council and the Council of States, observed during sessions. The point of comparison indicated by Rasch is their usual rest: during those periods, they sleep about 50 minutes less than usual. This distinction makes it possible to read the result without turning it into a general measure of the sleep of all people living in Switzerland.
For those who follow parliamentary work, the concrete question is not merely whether a representative remains awake in the chamber. It is whether fatigue can affect the assessment of information and the level of risk of decisions, as Rasch argues. The opportunity for a brief nap is presented precisely as a possibility for recovery during the day, intended to address that problem before fatigue affects efficiency.
### Duration and quality of rest
The source does, however, highlight that getting little sleep is not the only factor to consider. Sessions are often accompanied by aperitifs at which alcoholic drinks are present. Alcohol, the expert explains, can make it easier to fall asleep, but in the second half of the night it promotes more frequent and prolonged awakenings. The result can therefore be less restorative sleep, even when falling asleep seems easier.
A similar line of reasoning applies to sleeping pills. They help people fall asleep, but do not guarantee restorative rest. The survey shows that only a minority of parliamentarians use them, in line with the general population. The power nap, alcohol and sleeping pills are therefore not presented as equivalent: the first is a daytime recovery break, while the other two elements concern the quality of nighttime rest.
The reference to salute broadens the discussion beyond the Federal Palace. Rasch links sleep disorders to the level of stress and a higher risk of burnout in subsequent years, while calling for greater attention in schools to children and adolescents. The national angle of the proposal therefore lies in the relationship between rest conditions, parliamentary decisions and attention to health strategy, not in the introduction of a new rule already described in the source.

To turn the news into an orderly verification, the reader can follow a precise sequence without confusing the proposal with a decision already made.
### Four useful steps
- Separate evidence and proposal. The evidence is the study conducted on 16 members of the National Council and the Council of States; the proposal is to create spaces for short naps at the Federal Palace. - Correctly attribute the effects. The source reports that, according to Rasch, tired people tend to make riskier decisions and have more difficulty assimilating information. This is the researcher's assessment linked to the study data. - Examine sleep quality. It is necessary to distinguish the duration of rest from the elements described in the source: alcohol can help one fall asleep but favor awakenings in the second half of the night; sleeping pills do not ensure restorative rest. - Follow the two paths indicated by Rasch. The first concerns recovery spaces for parliamentarians; the second concerns greater attention to sleep in the national health strategy and in schools, especially for children and adolescents.
This reading procedure avoids two errors. The first is presenting power naps as a measure already implemented in Parliament. The second is turning the reference to sleeping pills into a recommendation: the source describes their use as a minority practice and does not propose doses, therapies or medical instructions.
For those following federal institutions, the point to check in any developments is therefore the distinction between a proposal by Rasch and an actual measure. The news provides data on sleep during sessions, indicates possible consequences for decisions and raises the issue of the health strategy and schools. These are the three elements to keep separate when assessing the continuation of the debate.

In the Canton of Solothurn, the search for inheritance and gift tax rates must start with the competent authority, not a federal table. The point is clear: Switzerland has no federal inheritance and gift tax.
### The correct scope
The Swiss tax system is structured at three levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal. However, this general framework should not be applied automatically to inheritance and gift matters. For this tax, responsibility lies exclusively with the canton and municipalities. The canton sets its own law and rates; the municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax.
Direct federal tax, or IFD, concerns income and wealth and is not the federal level of inheritance or gift tax. This distinction prevents attributing to AFC/ESTV a responsibility it does not have in this area: AFC/ESTV is responsible for IFD and VAT, while cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxes.
For anyone searching for the phrase inheritance and gift tax canton Solothurn rates, the practical consequence is to read the canton's rules without automatically transferring values or rules from another level. Rates by degree of kinship must be tied to the applicable cantonal legislation. The same caution applies to any exemptions relating to spouses and descendants: they should not be turned into a uniform Swiss-wide exemption without a cantonal basis.
UFAS/BSV and UST/BFS have different areas of responsibility: the former concerns social security, while the latter concerns statistics and does not set rates. To separate the ordinary calculation from verification of the inheritance or gift case, one can consult dichiarazione delle imposte, while still carrying out the specific verification with the competent cantonal administration. Practical difficulty lies not only in finding a percentage, but in understanding which tax level one is looking at. Each canton has its own law and multiplier. For this reason, a nationwide comparison cannot use the Canton of Solothurn as if it were a single Swiss-wide rate.
### How to interpret a rate
In a hypothetical scenario, anyone navigating inheritance and gifts should distinguish three elements. The first is the type of transaction. The second is the degree of kinship provided for under the applicable rules. The third is the municipality linked to the cantonal calculation. This sequence prevents adding a percentage of IFD to a levy that has no federal level.
The degree of kinship cannot be considered in isolation. If a table concerns spouses, descendants or other family relationships, it must be checked against the law of the Canton of Solothurn. The same caution applies to any exemptions: a rule attributed to another canton does not automatically become valid in Solothurn. The correct comparison starts with the cantonal text and then considers the municipal multiplier indicated for the local level.
The municipal multiplier has a specific role: it is applied to the cantonal amount. It is not a new federal tax and does not bring the matter under the jurisdiction of AFC/ESTV. Therefore, the data to be verified is not only the cantonal rate indicated in a fact sheet, but also how the municipality affects the cantonal result. Without this distinction, an estimate may confuse law, rate and multiplier.
Other levies and contributions should also not be mixed into the matter. AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG belong to social security. LAMal/KVG is compulsory health insurance for residents, with per-capita premiums, and is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. These elements do not replace the inheritance or gift tax rate and are not used to determine the degree of kinship.
For a separate ordinary calculation, calcolatore stipendio e imposte should be used within its scope; verification of inheritance or gift tax remains based on cantonal rules and the municipal multiplier.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. The practical procedure must follow the cantonal and municipal chain. It does not start with a federal office, because there is no federal level of taxation for inheritances and gifts.
### Five steps before submission
1. Classify the transaction. Indicate whether it is an inheritance or a gift. It should not be treated as an item of direct federal tax: IFD concerns income and wealth, whereas this matter falls under cantonal and municipal jurisdiction.
2. Establish the local scope. The case must be assigned to the Canton of Solothurn and the municipality concerned. The municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax, so the local check is not an optional step when interpreting the tax rate.
3. Verify the cantonal rule. The cantonal administration is the reference point for cantonal and municipal taxes. The request must concern the tax rate linked to the degree of kinship and any provisions for spouses and descendants, without replacing Solothurn's rules with those of another Canton.
4. Separate the competent offices. AFC/ESTV concerns IFD and VAT. UFAS/BSV concerns social security and UST/BFS statistics; neither of the latter two bodies sets inheritance or gift tax rates. This separation prevents the case from being sent to the wrong level.
5. Comply with the declaration and deadline. The declaration must be handled according to the instructions of the competent cantonal administration. It must not be replaced with a generic IFD deadline, because there is no federal tax on inheritances and gifts. Before submission, it is advisable to check that the tax rate, degree of kinship, municipality and multiplier all belong to the same cantonal scope.
The procedure for dichiarazione delle imposte serves to keep the ordinary tax part organized; it does not eliminate the specific verification required by Solothurn's rules. For a separate verification of ordinary taxes, open calcolatore stipendio e imposte.

item.title: Health insurance premiums, readers vent: «The same words every year»
item.description: In Ticino, the premium increase for 2027 is among the most limited, but the average premium exceeds 500 francs. The cumulative increase over four years would exceed 40%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 2027 premiums: in Ticino, the increase is among the most limited - The average premium remains above 500 francs per month - The cumulative increase over four years would exceed 40% - The 10% cap: starts in 2027, fully in place in 2028
- Location → Ticino - Subject → health insurance premiums for 2027 - Increase under discussion → 3,7% or 5% - Average premium → over 500 francs per month; 520 in the quoted comment - Cumulative increase → over 40% in the last four years - Cap → 10%; partial application in 2027 and full application in 2028 - DSS → Raffaele De Rosa - SUVA → reference point in the comparison on the single health insurance fund
SAVOSA - After the announcement of the premiums for 2027, comments expressing anger, irony and concrete proposals, in some cases extreme, appeared on the tio.ch blog. The common thread is the feeling that the same words return every year, while the discussion remains anchored to the monthly premium.
In Ticino, the percentage increase is among the lowest in the Confederation. The news, however, is not enough to reassure: the average premium remains the highest in Switzerland and exceeds 500 francs per month. One reader translates that level into an average of 520 francs per month and shifts attention from the percentage to how the system works.
### When the percentage comparison is not enough
> «The problem is no longer whether the increase is 3,7% or 5%,» writes one reader.
Another comment takes the basic policy of the reader's own insurer as a reference: the premium would rise from 445,95 to 468,25 francs, i.e. 5% more. The same report claims that the funds increasing the most are the cheaper ones, those chosen by people who need to save money.
The comments also point out that subsequent increases are not added together as isolated values. Each new percentage is calculated on a premium that has already increased in previous years; hence the estimate that the cumulative increase over the last four years would exceed 40%. Several readers therefore do not see the encouraging signal referred to by DSS head Raffaele De Rosa.
The second front concerns the initiatives voted on by Ticino residents. At the center is the 10% cap, whose implementation is described as unclear. According to the comments, part of it should enter into force in 2027 and the rest in 2028. The measure, some readers explain, limits the share borne by citizens but does not lower healthcare costs: the difference should be covered by the canton. To compare the points in the debate on cassa malati, the starting point remains the relationship among premium, percentage and timetable. ## The real weight of the premium in the balance sheet
Comparing percentages does not exhaust the examination of a policy. It is necessary to side by side the previous and the next premium, then read the percentage on the basis already increased. The example from 445.95 to 468.25 francs makes visible the difference between percentage number and monthly figure.
This method avoids mechanically summing annual increases. If the base changes each time, the final result follows a progression other than simple addition; the readers' estimate of 40% in four years stems from this reading. For costo della vita, the point is not only to determine whether a year's figure is low or high, but to understand from which premium one starts and what amount remains after the increase.
### A measure that shifts the problem
The roof discussed by the Ticinese must also be read by distinguishing two floors. On the one hand, there is the fee paid directly by citizens; on the other, there are the costs of health. The comments claim that the measure acts on the first floor and leaves the second unchanged, entrusting the Canton with the coverage of the difference. This is why some readers consider it a protection for those who pay, not a reduction in the overall cost.
The proposals on cuts intervene on different levers. Those who ask to close hospitals talk about the facilities in Ticino; those who propose to exclude private facilities or unnecessary services reason about the basic coverage. The abolition of the insurance obligation would change the perimeter of the system.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to turn comments into a verification
### Five practical steps
1. Start with the monthly amount. Note the premium shown on the policy and the one indicated after the update. The percentage alone does not replace the comparison with the average level above 500 francs or with the 520-franc reference that emerged in the comments. The comparison must remain anchored to the actual figures of one’s own situation.
2. Reconstruct previous years. Do not automatically add the percentages: apply each increase to the premium already increased in the previous year. This way you can compare the sequence of the four years with the over 40% indicated in the comments, without confusing an annual figure with the cumulative total.
3. Mark the initiative’s timetable. For the 10% cap, distinguish the partial entry into force planned for 2027 from the full one indicated for 2028. Then ask yourself which item is being limited: according to the explanation provided, the share borne by citizens, not healthcare costs. The difference would remain the Canton’s responsibility.
4. Classify the proposals before judging them. A fact sheet can keep hospitals, private facilities, unnecessary services, mandatory insurance, and specialists’ fees and salaries separate. These are ideas that emerged from readers, not a single plan: separating them prevents attributing to the source a decision that is not described.
5. Compare the two arguments concerning a single fund. On one hand, record the greater strength in price negotiations and the reference to SUVA; on the other, the administrative share indicated as between 3% and 4% and the doubt about the same premium throughout Switzerland. The result will be a readable assessment, not a choice based on a single percentage.
This process makes it possible to keep the monthly amount, cumulative effect, timetable, and reform proposals separate. To include the increase in the budget alongside income, use calcolatore stipendio.

According to Il Centro, however, the cantons cannot act alone. The Confederation should strengthen the tools available to address oversupply and excessive increases in spending. The same approach is set out in the five-point plan presented by Centro svizzero: strengthen primary care, orient remuneration more strongly toward quality and results, fully implement the electronic patient record and increase prevention efforts.
> «Containing the growth of costs does not mean reducing necessary care or weakening the quality of our healthcare system».

The consequence for interpreting upcoming announcements is concrete: it is necessary to look at both the amount of premiums and the type of intervention proposed. On 29 September 2026, from Bern, the Federal Office of Culture (UFC) announced support, for 2027 and 2028, for 26 provenance research projects concerning museums and collections in Switzerland. The total allocation is approximately 1,95 million francs.
The UFC received 30 applications. The supported projects were submitted as part of a public call and subsequently reviewed by the UFC. The support is granted within the framework of the Culture Message 2025–2028 and on the basis of the Federal Act on the Promotion of Culture, referred to in the source as LPCu.
### A multifaceted funding scheme
The call was also intended to reach museums and collections that had so far had little experience with provenance research. The projects include initiatives that bring together holdings from multiple museums, collaborations with partner institutions and communities of origin, analyses of human remains from colonial contexts, cataloguing of archives and data collection.
The research therefore does not follow a single format. Some projects concern the origin of holdings; others aim to make archives and data accessible for further research. Systematic preliminary assessments are also planned, useful for examining and documenting entire holdings and identifying areas requiring further investigation.
The source also links collaboration with institutions in the countries of origin to the possibility of initiating dialogue with a view to potential restitutions and to the future management of the holdings. It does not announce restitutions that have already taken place; instead, it describes a basis for work and dialogue. The list of supported projects 2027/2028 is indicated as an attachment, published on 28 September 2026. ### From the entire collection to the targeted investigation
For institutions, the most practical distinction is between an initial review of the entire collection and an investigation focused on problems already identified. Systematic preliminary assessments make it possible to examine and document entire collections, then identify and set priorities among the areas that need further assessment. The press release thus provides a basis for determining where to focus subsequent work.
When a gap in provenance has already been identified, or when an acquisition has a problematic context, in-depth research proceeds through further targeted investigations. Cataloguing and digitization follow a complementary logic: they make archives and data collections accessible for further research. The supported activities therefore cover both the examination of collections and the organization of the materials needed to continue the research.
### Collaborations and possible restitutions
The source also points to projects that bring together the collections of multiple museums or involve partner institutions and communities of origin. The work is not described solely as an internal analysis of the collections: collaboration with institutions in the countries of origin lays the foundations for dialogue with a view to possible restitutions and the future management of the collections.
The term possible qualifies the announced outcome. The press release does not present a restitution that has already been decided, but rather a process of gaining knowledge and engaging in dialogue that may provide a basis for further steps. The same applies to human remains from colonial contexts, which are included among the areas covered by the supported projects.
For the Swiss public, the verifiable point remains the work on the collections: the source speaks of new knowledge about the origin of the collections and of foundations for further investigations. The reported figure is a total of around 1,95 million francs for the 26 projects. Anyone who wants to keep this figure separate from their daily expenses can consult the costo della vita in Svizzera.

item.title: Swiss workers and AI: 28% use it but it does not convince them
item.description: 28% of workers in Switzerland use AI every day, but confidence is lacking. Data from PwC's 2026 'Hopes and Fears' research on employees.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 66% feel secure in their jobs for the next twelve months - 28% use generative AI every day in Switzerland - Only 10% see improved work quality - The Swiss survey involved 1000 employees
## Key facts - Research → 'Hopes and Fears' by PwC - Edition → 2026 - Swiss sample → 1000 employees - Period → between May and June - Daily AI use → 28% in Switzerland, 22% global average - Trust in direct supervisor → 21% - Negative culture as a reason to reject a job → 54% - Global survey → around 50'000 workers in 48 countries
66% of the Swiss workers surveyed feel secure in their jobs for the next twelve months, but only 27% are optimistic about demand for their skills in three years. This is the picture outlined by the new edition of PwC's 'Hopes and Fears' research, reported by Keystone-ATS.
### Daily use does not equate to confidence
Switzerland presents a paradox when it comes to generative artificial intelligence. 28% of respondents say they use it every day, compared with a global average of 22%. However, adoption does not automatically translate into a positive assessment: 14% feel motivated or more confident thanks to the tool, 10% see a clear improvement in work quality, no more than 9% believe it fosters skills and creativity, and only 22% say it helps them manage more complex tasks. PwC describes the result as AI use in Switzerland that still fails to convince many workers.
The research also measures the relationship with management. Only 21% trust their direct supervisor and 17% trust senior management; just 19% clearly know which skills will be required in the future. By contrast, employees value company culture, flexibility and autonomy: 54% cite a negative culture as a reason to reject a job, while 40% oppose greater control in the workplace.
Teena Madhvani, a PwC Switzerland executive quoted in a press release, observes that job security and salary are not enough to attract and retain talent. Trust, a strong company culture, genuine flexibility and transparent development opportunities are needed. Regarding AI, the executive also points out that use alone does not create acceptance: staff need support and targeted training in order to turn the tool into real productivity, measurable benefits and a better work experience.
In the 2026 edition, 1000 employees in Switzerland were interviewed between May and June. The global survey involved approximately 50'000 workers in 48 countries. ## What it means for daily work
The practical reading of the results starts from a precise gap: perceived short-term security is higher than optimism about the skills required in the medium term. For those who earn their living from their work in Switzerland, the question is not only whether AI is already present, but whether it produces a tangible benefit in the work being performed. The research data in fact distinguish three dimensions: frequency of use, perceived benefit and trust in the organization.
### A useful comparison between different signals
| Research signal | Practical reading | |---|---| | Daily use of generative AI | The presence of the tool alone does not demonstrate a benefit | | Improvement in quality and management of complex tasks | Usefulness must be verified in the actual work | | Skills required in the future | Clarity about professional expectations remains decisive | | Culture, flexibility and autonomy | Organizational conditions weigh in the choice of a job |
This distinction changes the way a job is evaluated. A worker may encounter an environment in which AI is used every day, but without greater motivation, trust, quality or ability to tackle complex tasks. In that case, adoption is an operational fact, not yet an advantage recognized by the staff. The research shows that frequent use and tangible benefit do not coincide.
The same logic applies to personnel management. Job security and salary remain elements cited by PwC, but they do not exhaust what employees assess. Trust in one's superior, transparency about future skills, company culture, flexibility and autonomy form a single package. Greater control in the workplace, if perceived as contrary to autonomy, can become a source of opposition, as indicated by the 40% identified by the survey.
For those comparing opportunities, annunci di lavoro are only the starting point: it is worth reading each proposal also through the lens of support, training, development and work organization, that is, the aspects highlighted by the research. For companies, the message is the reverse: AI can be introduced, but its acceptance requires conditions that staff recognize as credible. To attract and retain talent, according to PwC, more than simple job security and salary are needed.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to turn research into a personal assessment
Research findings can become a concrete assessment for people at work, without confusing the presence of AI with its value. The process can be organized into four steps, each linked to the criteria highlighted by PwC. The goal is to connect the tool to work outcomes, not to assume its benefit is automatic.
### Four operational steps
1. Separate frequency from benefit. Note whether generative AI is used every day and, separately, verify whether its use improves the quality of work, supports motivation, or increases trust. The research considers these effects separately.
2. Measure the outcome on the task. Check whether the quality of work improves, whether skills and creativity are fostered, and whether it becomes easier to manage complex tasks. These are the three tests indicated by the research data; if they do not emerge, use remains without a concrete benefit for people at work.
3. Ask for targeted support and training. PwC's comment identifies these two levers as necessary to turn AI into real productivity, measurable benefits, and a better work experience. They should therefore be focused on before considering the introduction of the tool a result.
4. Assess the work environment. When comparing one job with another, include trust, company culture, flexibility, autonomy, transparency about future skills, and level of control in the assessment. These are the factors that the research links to employee preferences.
Anyone evaluating a change can use the aziende che assumono as a point of comparison and ask specific questions about these aspects, without stopping at the mere presence of AI. Those who remain in their current job can apply the same four checks to their daily work and distinguish what is already measurable from what requires support or training.

## In brief - The USS calls for a legislative brake on basic health insurance premiums. - The motion sets a 3% limit on growth. - Above 3%, the USS proposes social or income taxes. - In Ticino, an increase of 3,7% is indicated in 2027.
## Key facts - Who → Swiss Trade Union Federation (USS) - Where → Bern - Proposal → Growth limited to 3% - Consideration → Tomorrow by the Council of States - Ticino → Increase of 3,7% in 2027
In Bern, the Swiss Trade Union Federation (USS) is calling for a legislative brake on the growth of basic health insurance premiums. According to the organization, for many households the burden has reached the limit of what is tolerable. The unions describe the current system as detrimental to citizens, conducive to waste and inequality, with effects also on the national economy.
In today's statement, the USS acknowledges that high-quality healthcare accessible to all comes at a cost. However, it challenges the way that cost is financed. In its view, hundreds of millions of francs from premiums are squandered for profit and dissipated in inefficient processes.
> «However, it is certainly not a law of nature that it should be financed in such an antisocial way, with hundreds of millions of francs from premiums being squandered for profit and dissipated in inefficient processes».
### The motion and the proposed limit The central point is the motion by USS President Pierre-Yves Maillard, which will be considered tomorrow by the Council of States. According to the federation, Parliament could amend the law and limit the growth of premiums, for example to 3%. The source therefore presents 3% as a limit to be introduced through a legislative decision.
For increases exceeding the threshold, the USS points to a different financing channel: social or income-based taxes, instead of per-capita premiums deemed antisocial. The related material also indicates that in Ticino the increase in premiums for 2027 will be 3,7%. The union describes the current situation as harmful to health policy, unsustainable for social policy and absurd for economic policy. If people are forced to save on premiums at the expense of their livelihood, the USS argues, the national economy also suffers. The postponement of care due to the share borne by insured persons, the organization concludes, may ultimately increase costs for everyone. For households, the issue is not only how much an expense grows, but how it is distributed. The basic health insurance premium is per capita, while the union proposal asks that increases beyond the threshold be financed through social or income-linked taxes. The debate therefore touches on the cost of living: it compares an individual outlay with income-linked financing.
Under the LAMal/KVG framework, basic insurance is mandatory for residents; premiums are organized by canton or region and premium reductions are cantonal. Cantons thus enter the practical reading of the topic, even if the political source explicitly cites mainly Bern and Ticino. To follow the perimeter of health spending one can consult LAMal/cassa malati, while the broader picture is that of cost of living in Switzerland.
### Three scenarios for the budget | Scenario | Practical reading | |---|---| | Current system | The premium remains a per capita expense linked to cost increases. | | 3% cap | The progression of premiums would have the limit indicated by the motion. | | Above the threshold | The excess share would be financed, in the USS proposal, with social or income-linked taxes. |
The proposed cap would not eliminate the cost of healthcare, which the USS itself acknowledges. Instead, it would change the way the increase is distributed. For a family, the possible effect would be a more contained growth of the individual premium, accompanied however by a different financing channel for the excess part. The source does not indicate additional amounts nor an already approved measure: the comparison therefore concerns an existing setup and a political scenario.
The health repercussion is equally concrete. If the weight of premiums pushes to reduce necessary expenses for subsistence, the pressure shifts to daily life. If it leads to postponing care, the cost can increase for everyone. This is the link that leads the USS to consider the issue not only social, but also economic and health.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. Anyone who wants to turn the news into a personal check can follow a simple sequence, without confusing the premium paid, the USS's request and any potential new financing criterion.
### Checklist for reading the updates 1. Start with the individual figure. Note the basic health insurance premium that affects the household budget. The comparison must start from the actual expenditure, not from a generic figure referring to Switzerland.
2. Check the parliamentary stage. The motion by USS president Pierre-Yves Maillard will be considered tomorrow by the Council of States. The 3% should therefore be read as the limit requested by the proposal, not as a threshold presented by the source as already applied.
3. Separate out the regional figure. The 3,7% indicated for 2027 concerns the increase in premiums in Ticino. It should not automatically be turned into a value valid for all cantons or for every household.
4. Assess the possible financing channel. In the model supported by the USS, increases above 3% should be financed with social or income-related taxes. This is the scenario indicated by the federation, not a new procedure already described as being in force.
This distinction makes it possible to follow the debate without confusing three levels: the expenditure that currently weighs on the budget, the threshold proposed by Parliament and the possible transfer of the excess portion. It also helps to correctly understand the relationship between livelihood and health described by the USS. If the premium leads people to forgo care or to turn to health services too late, the consequence indicated by the source concerns society as a whole.
