item.title: Health insurance 2027: a difference of up to 10'000 francs
item.description: In 2027, the national average will be 16'450 francs, but the difference between Geneva and Zug for the same family is close to 10'000 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- In 2027 the average Swiss family will be around 16’450 francs. - In Geneva the bill will approach 22’000 francs a year. - In Ticino the typical family will pay 21’346 francs. - There is a difference of almost 10’000 francs between the most expensive and least expensive canton.
## Key facts
- Typical family → two adults, one young person and one minor - Year → 2027 - National average → around 16’450 francs - Ticino → 21’346 francs - Geneva → almost 22’000 francs - Basel-Stadt → 20’458 francs - Zug and Appenzell Innerrhoden → 11’702-11’988 francs a year - Maximum difference → almost 10’000 francs a year
In 2027, a family consisting of two adults, one young person and one minor will spend an average of around 16’450 francs on health insurance premiums. The calculation was made based on the premiums announced today, Wednesday, by the Federal Office of Public Health, the FOPH. The national figure, however, conceals very wide differences between the various regions of Switzerland.
### The premium ranking
Geneva is at the top of the ranking: a typical family will have to budget for almost 22’000 francs a year in 2027, net of any subsidies. It is followed by Ticino, with 21’346 francs, and Basel-Stadt, with 20’458. These are the three most expensive cantons in the Confederation and the only ones to exceed the 20’000-franc threshold.
At the opposite extreme are Zug and Appenzell Innerrhoden. For two parents and two children, the annual premium remains below 1’000 francs a month, and the annual total indicated for these two cantons is between 11’702 and 11’988 francs. The source thus describes a gap of close to 10’000 francs between the most expensive canton and the most affordable one, for the same LAMal coverage.
For many households, a similar sum is equivalent to several months’ rent. The comparison with Grisons, however, narrows the gap to around 5’000 francs a year compared with the least expensive cantons. The geography of premiums therefore affects costo della vita in Svizzera and makes the canton of residence a decisive variable when drawing up the family budget.
The picture concerns not only the level of premiums, but also their evolution. The ranking of the increases announced for 2027 differs from that of overall costs: Ticino remains among the most expensive cantons, but does not record the steepest increase.
The data thus paint a picture of a Switzerland that is highly fragmented also when it comes to healthcare spending. The figures explain why the announcement of yet another increase reignites the debate over the need for a reform of the system. ## The level and the change do not coincide
To understand the impact on the household budget, two measures must be separated: how much is paid overall and how much it increases compared with this year. The Ticino case highlights the difference. A family residing in the Canton spends on average over 4’100 francs more than the Swiss average and almost 9’400 more than a family residing in Zug.
### The daily burden for families
Converted into a daily measure, spending in Ticino amounts to around 56 francs per day for basic health insurance. For a Zug family, it is around 31 francs: the gap is about 25 francs per day, more than many people spend on food, according to the comparison reported by the source. The figure makes the burden of premiums visible even when one does not look at the annual total.
The ranking changes when the increase expected for 2027 is considered. In Ticino, the additional cost for the typical family is estimated at 741 francs and 60 centimes, compared with a national average of around 801 francs. The increase in Ticino is around 3,6%, a significant rise but more contained than that observed in recent years and in several other Cantons.
### The strongest increases are elsewhere
The record for increases goes to Jura, with 1’067 francs more than this year for an average family. Solothurn, Schaffhausen and Neuchâtel are around 940 francs; Zurich also exceeds the national average. In Graubünden, however, the additional cost for 2027 remains below 600 francs.
For those preparing the budget, the comparison shows that a Canton can have high premiums overall and, at the same time, an annual increase below the average. The percentage or amount of the increase does not erase the starting level. It is this combination, together with the distance between regions, that fuels the debate over the need for a reform of the system. To navigate the healthcare item in the Swiss budget, the reference remains LAMal e cassa malati.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Four steps to reduce spending
The source indicates a concrete strategy for families who want to contain premiums: start by comparing, check the alternatives and verify possible access to subsidies. The process helps put one's own premium into the context of the canton where one lives.
### 1. Compare premiums
The first step is to compare the available premiums. The comparison must be based on the same insurance need, because the service compares families with identical LAMal coverage. Looking only at the national total is not enough: the source shows that spending varies greatly from one canton to another. The comparison must therefore be linked to the situation of one's household and place of residence.
### 2. Choose the cheapest health insurer
After the comparison, the advice is to choose the cheapest health insurer. This step turns the data into a budget decision: the annual premium can amount to many months' rent, especially in the cantons where spending is higher. The choice must be made without confusing the Swiss average with the amount applied in one's own region.
### 3. Assess the alternative models
The third check concerns the alternative models. The source lists them among the possibilities for reducing spending. In practical terms, it is advisable to compare the model's effect on the premium before settling on the first proposal and to keep the comparison based on the same LAMal coverage.
### 4. Check subsidies
Finally, it is necessary to verify whether one is entitled to subsidies. The service specifies that the amounts are shown net of any subsidies in the case of Geneva; for this reason, the check can change the way the household bill is understood. To follow the comparison between premi della cassa malati and your personal budget, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.description: The Federal Administration offers 50 vocational training programs, internships for recent graduates, and seven weeks of vacation.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Meaningful work and responsibility in the Federal Administration - Internships for recent graduates - 50 vocational training programs available - Seven weeks of vacation during vocational training
## Key facts - Internship recipients → recent graduates - Vocational training programs → 50 - Vacation during vocational training → 7 weeks - Employer offering → flexible work, performance-based remuneration and continuing education
The Federal Administration offers recent graduates a wide range of internships. The offer is presented as a way to gain valuable practical experience, expand one's network of contacts and use one's knowledge to help shape Switzerland's future. The message thus combines concrete experience and contribution to the community.
Work at the Federal Administration is described as meaningful. Those who work there can take on responsibility and work for the well-being of the population in Switzerland. The page also indicates the opportunity to develop innovative solutions within multidisciplinary teams. The stated aim is to make a concrete contribution to the high quality of life in the country.
### Three options presented by the page
Alongside internships, the text presents the offer for those seeking vocational training that is meaningful, fosters growth and opens up new opportunities. There are 50 programs available. The practical side is described precisely: those who follow these paths contribute to real tasks and projects, learn from the trainers who support them and develop skills for their future.
Leisure time also appears among the elements of the offer. The seven weeks of vacation are indicated as time to devote to relaxation, hobbies, travel and friends. This figure accompanies the description of vocational training and completes the picture together with practical learning.
The picture is completed by what the Federal Administration declares it offers as an employer: flexible forms of work, performance-based remuneration, continuing education and other offers. These are the elements with which the page describes the Federal Administration as an interesting employer.
For those reading the offer, the distinction is clear: the internship is linked to practical experience and networking; vocational training to tasks, projects and skills; work in the Administration to responsibility, innovative solutions and multidisciplinary collaboration. Anyone who wants to compare this offer with other positions can start from annunci di lavoro. ## From the offer to the choice
Those considering these opportunities must distinguish the type of experience they want to build. The page does not present a single format: it places internships for students who have recently graduated alongside the 50 vocational training programs and the conditions offered by the Federal Administration as an employer. The practical approach consists in linking each element to the personal objective, without confusing hands-on experience, training and employment conditions.
| Pathway | Elements indicated | |---|---| | Internships | hands-on experience, network of contacts and knowledge | | Vocational training | real tasks and projects, trainers and future skills | | Work in the Federal Administration | responsibility, innovative solutions and multidisciplinary teams |
For a student who has recently graduated, the point of comparison is the experience that the internship makes it possible to acquire in the field. The network of contacts and knowledge complete this pathway: they are not presented as separate elements, but as part of the contribution through which to build Switzerland's future.
For those seeking vocational training, the criterion is more closely linked to doing. Collaborating on real tasks and projects makes it possible to view the offer through the activities envisaged; the support provided by trainers, on the other hand, signals the accompanying component. Future skills and the seven weeks of vacation add, in the same description, a dimension of growth and personal time.
A third dimension concerns those who consider the Federal Administration as an employer. Here the page draws attention to forms of flexible work, performance-based remuneration, continuing education and other offers. These are criteria different from hands-on experience or choosing a training program, but they contribute to the overall description of the employment.
The comparison with other employers should be made while keeping these dimensions distinct: the content of the experience, learning methods and conditions offered. To broaden the search, one can consult aziende che assumono, without losing the concrete references indicated by the page.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to navigate the opportunities
### Four practical steps
The first step consists of defining which element one wants to look for. The page brings together meaningful work, responsibility, contribution to the well-being of the population and the opportunity to develop innovative solutions in multidisciplinary teams. If these are the main points of reference, the reader can focus on the description of work in the Federal Administration.
The second step is to check whether one's goal is related to an internship. For recent graduates, the option to consider is a wide range of internships, with three stated outcomes: hands-on experience, a network of contacts and the use of one's knowledge to help build Switzerland's future.
The third step concerns vocational training. Here, it is advisable to start from the 50 possibilities available and look for the path that combines real tasks and projects, support from trainers and the development of skills for the future. The seven weeks of vacation are part of the same assessment: the page links them to time for relaxation, hobbies, travel and friends.
The fourth step is to read the offer from the employer's point of view. Flexible forms of work, performance-based remuneration, continuing education and other offers are the elements to consider together when assessing the overall offering.
This method avoids conflating different paths. First, one identifies the area of interest, then compares the elements explicitly described and finally chooses the direction most consistent with what one is seeking: experience, training or working conditions. To assess the impact of remuneration on one's budget, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.description: From deputies dating back to 1848 to CN votes: how to use the official portal to track acts, committees, and EU/NATO delegations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Parliament comprises the National Council and the Council of States - The portal lists members of parliament since 1848 - Curia Vista, voting records, and Open Data are among the tools - Delegations include EFTA, NATO, and OECD
## Key facts - Chambers → National Council and Council of States - Archive → Members of parliament since 1848 - Search → Curia Vista and advanced search - Data → Open Data and National Council voting database - Delegations → EFTA/EU, NATO AP, and OECD DP
## Parliament as an institutional map
The Swiss Parliament page highlights members of parliament since 1848 and pairs this section with the search for members of the two Chambers. The National Council and the Council of States each have their own Office, a president, A-to-Z member lists, search by Canton, seat arrangements, and changes in membership. The structure allows users to start from the person, the Chamber, or the composition of the body.
### Committees, groups, and delegations
Alongside the Chambers, the plenary session of the Federal Assembly is featured, with advanced search and information on its members. The committees section includes thematic committees, reports, items under consultation, and subcommittees. Among the oversight committees are the CFP and the CFF; the portal also lists special committees and other committees, including the Committee of Pardons, the Judicial Committee, and the National Council’s Committee on Immunity.
The catalog also reports on the CPI regarding the management of authorities in relation to the emergency merger of Credit Suisse with UBS and the inspection related to the COVID-19 pandemic. Reports, reference documents, and delegation activities are present. For international relations, entries include EFTA/EU, NATO AP, OECD DP, and permanent delegations to the parliaments of neighboring states.
The political section is completed by the UDC, Socialist, Center, PVL, Free Democratic, Green, and Green Liberal groups. To follow parliamentary work, the portal brings together votes, the National Council voting database, the Official Gazette, Curia Vista, sessions, elections, items, Open Data, and embed code for the live stream.
Navigation also includes the elections of the Federal Council, the Chancellors, and the judges of the Federal Courts, as well as the ratification of cantonal constitutions. In a separate section, the portal describes the Parliament Building, parliamentary services, and the history of the Parliament, including the renovation and restoration of the Parliament Building from 2006 to 2008. ## How to navigate parliamentary business and decisions
For people who live or work in Switzerland, the page is above all a navigation tool: it distinguishes members, sessions, items, committees, votes and documents.
The page also offers Contact and Easy language and lists the de, fr, it, rm and en versions. Before searching for an item, one can therefore choose the language access provided by the portal.
| Need | Suggested path | What it offers | |---|---|---| | Search for a parliamentarian | Members A–Z or Members by canton | list and seating arrangement | | Trace an item | Curia Vista and Advanced search | items, replies and documents | | Check a vote | National Council voting database | votes and xls files | | Read about parliamentary finances | Budget procedure | credits, limits and integrated plan |
### From dossier to verification
If the starting point is a parliamentarian, the sections devoted to the two Chambers make it possible to compare the alphabetical list with the canton, the seating arrangement and changes. If, instead, one is looking for an item, Curia Vista offers an advanced search and an explanation of the system; the portal also provides answers to parliamentary interventions and interventions containing tables or graphs.
Verification does not stop at the text of the item. The Official Bulletin has a section dedicated to explanations, and the portal presents the 125 years of the Official Bulletin of the Federal Assembly. For a vote in the National Council, the database and an xls file are available to download. Previous sessions, an overview of sessions in preview and a search for the Official Bulletin add further points of control.
For finance, the entries to be read together are financial planning, the budget procedure, financial management tools, types of credit and the spending limit, supplementary credits, and the budget with an integrated task and financial plan. This sequence helps distinguish the budget document, the credit and parliamentary oversight, without attributing to the individual page any content other than that indicated in the menu.
The same logic applies to oversight: reports, reference documents, oversight committees and the CPA evaluation process should be sought in their respective sections. At the external level, the EFTA/EU delegations, NATO PA and OECD PD distinguish international parliamentary relations from the activities of the Chambers. When it comes to the personal budget, dichiarazione delle imposte and costo della vita in Svizzera can be placed side by side, keeping the information tools distinct.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Practical Procedure for Using the Portal
Consultation can become a repeatable process. The criterion is to start from the specific question rather than opening all sections at once.
### Five Steps
1. Define the subject. Choose among member, vote, session, committee, delegation, or financial document. The menu distinguishes these categories.
2. Select the Chamber or body. For the National Council and the Council of States, use Office, President, Members A–Z, Canton, Seats, or Changes; for the plenary, use the dedicated entry and advanced search.
3. Search for the document. Use Curia Vista, advanced search, Subjects, or Sessions; for interventions, check responses and tables or charts.
4. Verify the track. For votes, compare the National Council database, the Official Gazette, and explanations; for finance, consult the budget, credits, limits, additional appropriations, and the integrated plan.
5. Follow the format. Previous sessions, preview overview, Open Data, xls files, and the embed code for the stream address different needs.
After the search, note whether the content belongs to a committee, a group, or a delegation. The portal keeps thematic, oversight, and special committees distinct from parliamentary groups and delegations. This separation helps avoid confusing a report with an oversight activity or a group position.
For external relations, the procedure ends at the relevant delegation: EFTA/EU, NATO PA, OECD DP, UIP, APF, DCE, or OSCE PA. For neighboring states, the menu refers to the permanent delegations and activities related to the German Bundestag, the French Parliament, the Italian Parliament, the Liechtenstein Landtag, and the Austrian Parliament. The correct path starts from the body and leads to the activity or legal basis indicated.
If the goal is to follow a sitting, start from the Sessions section and then check previous sessions or the preview overview. If a reusable format is needed, choose Open Data or the xls file; for the live broadcast, use the embed code provided by the portal.
To move from reading financial dossiers to verifying your own income, use the salary calculator.

item.title: Health insurance premiums 2027 in Ticino: +3,7% and EFAS from 2028
item.description: Lukas Engelberger: the system is good and costs money. In Ticino, premiums are rising by 3,7%, with EFAS expected from 2028.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2027, premiums in Ticino will increase by 3.7% - Lukas Engelberger: the healthcare system is good and therefore costly - EFAS should ease the burden on insured persons from 2028 - Pierre Maudet calls for measures at every level
## Key facts Date → 29 September 2026 Location → Bern Subject → 2027 health insurance premiums Increase in Ticino → 3.7% President of the CDC → Lukas Engelberger Vice President of the CDC → Pierre Maudet Measure from 2028 → EFAS Agency → Keystone-ATS
On 29 September 2026, in Bern, the announcement of health insurance premiums for 2027 brought the cost of the Swiss healthcare system to the forefront. Lukas Engelberger, president of the Conference of Cantonal Health Directors (CDC), summed up his position in one sentence: «The system is good, so it costs».
Engelberger argues that the Swiss system is good, but calls on politicians to curb the growth of the burden. He explains to the Keystone-ATS agency that the extensive catalogue of services covered by basic insurance benefits patients. In his reasoning, the benefit for insured persons coexists with a cost that politicians must contain. For those following premi di cassa malati, the point indicated by the president of the CDC is therefore the relationship between the breadth of services and the growth of the burden.
The figure indicated for Ticino is a 3.7% increase in premiums for 2027. The announcement is accompanied by reactions from parties and trade unions. Among the positions reported, USS maintains that a legislative brake on health insurance premiums is needed. The request also brings the issue of legislative action to contain premiums into the debate.
### EFAS from 2028
To ease the burden on insured persons, Engelberger is looking ahead to 2028 and the so-called EFAS, the uniform financing of services. According to the Centre representative, the model should entail greater financial responsibility for the Cantons. At the same time, it should improve the exchange of information and eliminate distorted incentives. The relief is therefore placed in the future indicated by the article, while the communication examined concerns the premiums for 2027.
### The levers identified by the CDC
Pierre Maudet, Vice President of the CDC, argues that measures are needed at every level. The Geneva State Councillor particularly highlights planning, quality and prevention. In his view, the cantonal authorities must have the data and tools necessary to manage costs better and eliminate the wrong incentives. The picture described thus brings together three aspects: the increase indicated for Ticino, the uniform financing associated with EFAS and the Cantons’ intervention in managing the healthcare system. ## Two horizons to keep separate
The practical reading of the news starts with a simple distinction: 2027 concerns the announcement of premiums, while 2028 is the year indicated for possible relief through EFAS. For insured persons, these are two different questions. The first is which burden to consider in the next premium cycle; the second is how the financing of benefits would change if the model produced the effects described by Engelberger. The relief indicated for 2028 therefore remains a prospect, not a reduction already available in 2027.
The reference to premi LAMal/KVG serves to avoid confusing healthcare expenditure with other items. Premiums are neither direct federal tax nor VAT, and do not coincide with AVS/AHV or LPP/BVG contributions; instead, they affect costo della vita in Svizzera. The news therefore remains within the domain of health insurance: it does not describe tax or social security changes. For the reader, the question concerns healthcare expenditure and how it is financed.
### The responsibility of the Cantons
The second practical step concerns the Cantons. If EFAS were to ease the burden on insured persons, Engelberger's position indicates greater financial responsibility for the Cantons. This element goes hand in hand with improved information exchange and the elimination of distorted incentives. Maudet's position adds three levers to observe: planning, quality and prevention. These are the points on which, in the text, the Cantons' ability to intervene in costs is measured.
For the reader, this changes how future news is assessed: a percentage alone is not enough; one must look for which institutional level is acting, which data it uses and whether the measure affects cost management. The USS's request for a legislative brake represents another avenue in the debate, distinct from the cantonal levers indicated by the CDC. Reading premiums, EFAS and cantonal responsibility together avoids reducing the issue to the percentage figure alone.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## A practical sequence for finding your bearings
To turn the announcement into an operational reading, it is useful to follow five steps. The point is not to add figures, but to separate the reported data from the measures still described as a prospect.
### Five checks before deciding
1. Identify the scope. Start with the canton concerned and check whether the data you are reading concerns Ticino or another communication. In the available material, the reference for Ticino is 3,7% for 2027. Do not automatically turn this percentage into a national value.
2. Mark the time horizon. Keep 2027 separate from the date 2028 associated with EFAS. The first is the communicated premium cycle; the second is the prospect of uniform financing that should ease the burden on policyholders. This distinction prevents attributing an immediate effect to EFAS.
3. Read the levers. When assessing a cantonal decision, look for the three areas mentioned by Maudet: planning, quality and prevention. Use them as a framework to understand whether the measure addresses one of the fronts indicated by the CDC.
4. Check the method. The CDC points to the availability of data and tools to manage costs better and eliminate the wrong incentives. In a communication or analysis, therefore, check whether these two elements are explained: this is the operational criterion offered by the text.
5. Distinguish the proposals. The USS's request for a legislative brake belongs to the debate on reactions to premiums. The measures on planning, quality, prevention and tools instead belong to the cantonal level indicated by the CDC. Separating them helps to understand whether the discussion concerns legislation, management or uniform financing.

item.title: Real estate investments: good confidence, Ticino negative
item.description: In 2026, the SRESI stands at 47,5 points, down from 69,5 in 2025; Ticino and Lugano in negative territory, while Zurich, Central Switzerland and Lake Geneva lead expectations of increases.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - SRESI 2026: 47,5 points, compared with 69,5 in 2025 - Moderate price growth expected in Switzerland - Ticino and Lugano are in negative territory - Zurich, Central Switzerland and Lake Geneva lead
- Index → SRESI - Publication → annual, KPMG - Survey → approximately 370 specialists - Horizon → following twelve months - 2024 → 29,9 points - 2023 → -77,4 points, negative record - Highest value since 2012 → 69,5 points in 2025 - Economic center trending downward → Lugano
In 2026, the Swiss Real Estate Sentiment Index (SRESI) stood at 47,5 points, after 69,5 in 2025. Confidence in real estate investments remains good in Switzerland, but the figure is lower than the previous year and Ticino is moving in a different direction from the areas with the most favorable expectations.
The SRESI is published annually by KPMG and gathers experts' expectations regarding the sector's development over the following twelve months. The 2026 edition is based on a survey conducted among approximately 370 specialists. The series shows 29,9 points in 2024 and -77,4 in 2023, a negative record; 2025, on the other hand, was the highest value since 2012, the year from which the indicator has been calculated.
### A declining index, but not a turning point
> “The real estate investment market remains solid, despite moderate economic expectations,” comments Beat Seger, a KPMG expert, quoted in a press release.
According to Seger, the decline in the index does not signal a reversal in trend, but rather a normalization after the previous year, which had proved exceptionally strong. This interpretation explains why the 2026 result is lower than that of 2025 without being presented as a change in the market's direction.
### Differences on the Swiss map
The forecasts for the most marked price increases still concern Zurich, Central Switzerland and the Lake Geneva region. Lugano is instead the only economic center for which experts expect prices to decline, while Ticino as a whole is in negative territory.
The distance between these areas and Ticino is the clearest territorial feature of the survey. On the one hand, the national picture maintains a forecast of moderate price growth; on the other, the survey indicates a more cautious direction for the canton and a negative one for Lugano. The result is therefore not a ranking of current prices, but a map of specialists' expectations for the following twelve months. KPMG describes a real estate investment market that is still solid, despite moderate economic expectations. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical value of the index lies in the comparison between the national and local scales. The forecast of moderate price growth does not produce the same signal in every area: Ticino is indicated to be in negative territory, and Lugano is the only economic center with downward expectations. The correct reading therefore starts with the place to which the question refers.
The first step is to define the scope. National data describes Switzerland's overall outlook, but it does not replace the reading referring to Ticino. The third step is to read 2026 together with the previous year. ## In brief - The vote on the law is scheduled for 29 November. - The Federal Council wants to relax export rules. - The reform focuses on defence and jobs. - The proposal also concerns re-exports.
## Key facts - Vote: 29 November - Subject: revision of the War Material Act - Proponent: Federal Council - Objective: strengthen the defence industry and safeguard jobs - Current rule: ban on exports to countries involved in internal or international conflicts - New: greater leeway on exports and re-exports - Control: right of veto and retention in the purchasing country if there are reservations - Exceptions: exceptional circumstances, with international obligations respected
On 29 November, a vote will be held on the revision of the War Material Act backed by the Federal Council. The Government's call to approve it effectively opens the campaign for the referendum, which the source places exactly two months after the Executive's position. The stated objective is twofold: strengthen the defence industry and safeguard jobs.
The starting point is the regime currently in force. Switzerland bans the export of war material to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. According to Bern, since the start of the war between Russia and Ukraine, this rigidity has made the Swiss arms industry unattractive and subjected it to strong pressure.
### The leeway sought by Parliament
The bourgeois majority in Parliament wants to grant the Government greater leeway over exports and re-exports. The operational objective is to facilitate the transfer, by Western countries, of war material purchased in Switzerland to third countries. The proposal therefore concerns exports and re-exports.
The Federal Council should also be given a right of veto. The Government could also require the weapons to remain in the purchasing country when there are reservations about security or neutrality policy. In exceptional circumstances, to protect foreign-policy or security interests, it would be possible to depart from the current authorisation criteria, but only in compliance with international obligations.
The Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research presents the reform as a way to ensure greater flexibility in foreign policy during exceptional crises and to strengthen the Swiss arms industry as a foundation of national defence. Guy Parmelin, President of the Confederation and economics minister, invoked the guarantee of neutrality before Parliament.
> “The new regime will always be applied in strict compliance with Swiss neutrality and international law,” Guy Parmelin stressed before Parliament. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the proposal would primarily change how the Government could assess a sale or re-export. The source describes the new framework as a revision to be put to a vote, not as a rule already applicable. The comparison should therefore be read as a possible before and after, not as a change that has already entered into force.
### Before and after
Before, the stated rule is clear: Swiss war materiel cannot be exported to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. If approved, the Federal Council would have greater leeway, but within precise conditions.
| Element | Proposed measure | Control element | | Exports | Greater room for maneuver | Exceptions to the current criteria only in exceptional circumstances | | Re-exports | Facilitate Western transfers to third countries | Federal Council veto right | | Purchased weapons | Possible requirement to remain in the purchasing country | Reservations concerning security or neutrality | | Exceptions | Safeguarding foreign policy or security interests | Compliance with international obligations |
The table does not describe an automatic authorization. The proposal retains a direct role for the Federal Council and links decisions to security, neutrality policy, foreign policy interests and international obligations. The exception is also presented as a tool for exceptional circumstances, not as an ordinary rule.
The stated economic impact concerns the arms sector and jobs. However, the source does not quantify employees, wages, orders, companies involved or jobs that would be safeguarded. It therefore does not allow the political objective to be turned into a forecast of new hires or regional effects. To track the possible employment impact, annunci di lavoro is a useful reference point, but it does not replace the data that are absent from the source.
The key issue for the domestic audience is the combination of industrial appeal and state control. Bern wants to respond to the pressures reported after the start of the war between Russia and Ukraine; at the same time, the new regime should remain tied to Swiss neutrality and international law.

To follow the dossier without confusing a proposal with a law currently in force, it is advisable to use a simple sequence. The source does not indicate forms, individual applications or administrative procedures for workers and companies: the concrete step indicated is the vote on 29 novembre. The rest of the analysis must remain anchored to the criteria explicitly described.
### Five checks before the vote
1. Mark the deadline. 29 novembre is the date of the vote on the revision of the War Material Act. Do not add a year that the source does not indicate.
2. Establish the starting rule. Today, Swiss war material cannot be exported to countries involved in internal or international conflicts. This is the reference point for understanding the scope of the proposal.
3. Isolate the requested expansion. The bourgeois majority in Parliament wants more leeway for exports and re-exports, so as to facilitate transfers by Western countries to third countries.
4. Check the safeguards. The Federal Council should have a right of veto and could require that the weapons remain in the purchasing country if reservations arise regarding security or the policy of neutrality.
5. Verify the exceptions. Every derogation from the current criteria is linked to exceptional circumstances, the protection of foreign policy or security interests and compliance with international obligations.
This checklist also helps to read the economic statements with caution. The objective of strengthening the defense industry and safeguarding jobs is explicit; the source, however, provides no figures on companies, employees, wages or expected results. For a complete reading, it is advisable to consider together the two political documents mentioned by the source: the press release of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research and the position expressed by the Government before Parliament. The criterion to be verified remains the compatibility between greater flexibility, Swiss neutrality and international law.

item.title: 2027 Premium Increase: Reactions from the PLR, PS, and Unions
item.description: Estimate at 3,7% for 2027. PLR calls for cost control, PS and OCST defend families. Average Ticino premium at 519,90 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In Brief - 3.7%: Estimated increase in Ticino premiums for 2027 - 519.90 francs: Highest average premium ever - 10%: Initiative approved by the Ticino people - January 1, 2027: First stage of the initiative
## Key Facts - What → Increase in health insurance premiums - Estimate → 3.7% - Year → 2027 - Location → Ticino - Average premium → 519.90 francs - Initiative → 10% - Approval → September 28, 2025 - First stage → January 1, 2027
On September 29, 2026, an estimate of 3.7% was given for the increase in health insurance premiums in Ticino in 2027. This figure is lower than in recent years. and lower than the national average, but it doesn't eliminate the bitterness of yet another price increase. At 519.90 francs, the canton remains the one with the highest average premium overall.
The announcement provoked reactions from political parties and unions, with differing approaches. The FDP considers the trend of increases unsustainable and shifts the focus from the discussion on how to offset the increase to the causes of rising healthcare costs. For readers who want to delve deeper into the topic, the dossier cassa malati offers a consistent entry point to the announcement.
> "The principle for the FDP is simple: if we want to curb premiums, we must curb the growth of healthcare costs."
### The parties' demands
In the Grand Council, the party called for a cantonal strategy based on cost monitoring, measurable objectives, and a more effective use of supply planning. It also highlighted the strong growth of physiotherapy centers, private Spitex services, and independent nurses, calling for transparency and rigor. The FDP also links this work to tax breaks and subsidies, hospital planning, and increased efficiency in the healthcare system. At the federal level, the motion "Quality over Quantity," resubmitted on September 29, 2026, calls for prioritizing the outcome of care over the number of tests, treatments, and surgeries. The party also points to EFAS, increased competition, and interventions on drug prices.
The SP views the price increase as a direct blow to Ticino households, along with rent, energy, and fuel. It calls for increased subsidies and a reduction in healthcare costs. It cites the 10% Initiative, approved by the Ticino electorate on September 28, 2025: the first stage will come into force on January 1, 2027. Regarding hospital control, the party points to delays in the new planning, points out that the Grand Council is still awaiting the messages on the most recent annual reports from the EOC, and notes that no report on the performance mandates of private institutions has yet been submitted to Parliament. Finally, the OCST insists on a substantially fixed income and on the sacrifices that can accumulate, from dinner to cultural activities, to helping children and grandchildren. ### Two Levels to Separate
A practical interpretation of the 2027 estimate requires two comparisons. In terms of pace, the increase is more moderate than in recent years and below the national average. At the starting level, however, the average premium in Ticino remains the highest overall. The first information puts the change into perspective; the second explains why the increase continues to weigh on budgets. The useful comparison is therefore not just between percentages, but between the announced change and the average value already indicated for the canton.
The SP and the OCST describe the same pressure from the perspective of households, families, and retirees: wages and incomes are not growing at the same rate, while rent, energy, fuel, and the cost of living are increasingly important in budgets. The OCST translates this pressure into daily choices: a dinner, a vacation, a cultural activity, or help for children or grandchildren. This sequence is presented not as a single sacrifice, but as a sum of sacrifices that diminish the quality of life year after year. To compare the points cited in the debate, you can also use the costo della vita in Svizzera guide.
### Cost Relief and Control
The positions gathered can be read on two levels, without overlapping:
| Plan | Elements at the heart of the debate | Indicated objective | |---|---|---| | Support for families | subsidies and the 10% Initiative | easing the burden on budgets | | Healthcare costs | monitoring, measurable objectives, and supply planning | containing spending growth | | Hospitals | planning, control, and transparency for public and private institutions | making data and financial flows legible | | Federal level | Quality over quantity, EFAS, competition, and drug prices | addressing volume, incentives, and prices |
This distinction helps understand why the debate isn't limited to percentage figures. Subsidies are presented as a tool to relieve families; monitoring, objectives, planning, and transparency, on the other hand, concern spending growth and supply control. The PLR argues that shifting the burden from insured persons to taxpayers will not make it easier, while the SP calls for action on both fronts.
The hospital dossier is where these demands converge. Planning, EOC reports, performance mandates for private institutions, and financial flows are identified as areas requiring greater transparency, oversight, and collaboration between the government and parliament. The debate involves the Grand Council and the Council of State; the federal level appears with the motion "Quality over Quantity," "EFAS," competition, and drug prices.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### A checklist for following the next steps
The discussion offers some concrete references for those who want to follow the evolution of premiums without confusing support measures with cost control. The following sequence remains anchored to the dates, bodies and dossiers cited by Ticino’s political forces.
1. Mark the date. January 1, 2027 is the date indicated for the entry into force of the first stage of the 10% Initiative, approved on September 28, 2025 by the people of Ticino. It is the first temporal reference to keep separate from the interventions still under discussion. 2. Divide the measures by objective. Under relief measures, include the Initiative and the strengthening of subsidies requested by the PS. Under costs, note monitoring, measurable objectives and supply planning, requested by the PLR. This distinction makes a decision understandable without attributing effects to it that differ from those declared. 3. Follow the cantonal work. The point to verify is the progress of the strategy to contain healthcare spending requested in the Grand Council: cost monitoring, measurable objectives and more effective use of planning. These are the three elements indicated by the PLR for moving from announcement to structured control. 4. Check the hospital dossier. The PS’s requests include greater timeliness in hospital planning, greater transparency in overseeing public and private institutions, data on financial flows and collaboration between the Government and Parliament. The dossier also continues to include the EOC’s annual reports and the service mandates of private institutions. 5. Measure the pressure to give things up. The OCST cites dinner, vacation, cultural activities and help for children or grandchildren. Using these items as budget categories makes it possible to observe the reduction in quality of life described by the union, while keeping the focus on the categories cited.
To follow developments, it is advisable to distinguish each communication between subsidies, spending containment, hospital planning and federal proposals. The motion Quality instead of quantity, EFAS, competition and medicine prices in fact belong to a different level from the requests addressed to the Grand Council and the State Council.

item.description: Status of work on railway stations and bus stops in Switzerland updated according to the Federal Office of Transport.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 1168 railway stations accessible by the end of 2025 - 83 per cent of travelers benefit from the adaptations - 50 per cent of bus stops can be used - 250 million francs for 2025–2028
## Key facts - Publication → 29 September 2026 - Authority → Federal Office of Transport (UFT) - Railways → 1168 out of approximately 1800 stations and stops - Buses → approximately 25 000 stops - Obligation → Disability Act (LDis), by the end of 2023 - Planning by the end of 2029 → 193 stations and stops - Funding 2025–2028 → 250 million francs - Condition → proportionate intervention
On 29 September 2026, from Bern, the Federal Office of Transport (UFT) indicated in its latest report on the progress of the work that, at the end of 2025, people with disabilities could independently use 1168 of the approximately 1800 railway stations and stops in Switzerland. This figure is up by 36 from the previous year.
### Railways: passenger figures
The number of adapted stations does not correspond to the share of passengers affected. The larger stations were the first to undergo structural modernization: as a result, the renovations carried out to meet the needs of people with disabilities could be used by 83 per cent of all passengers. Current planning provides for another 193 stations and stops to be adapted by the end of 2029, with the share of benefiting passengers expected to rise to at least 87 per cent.
Under the Disability Act (LDis), railway companies and the owners of the roads had to renovate their stations and stops by the end of 2023 so that people with disabilities could use them independently. However, this obligation was subject to the proportionality of the intervention.
The UFT monitors implementation and requires interim measures for delayed projects, ensuring a uniform and proper assessment of proportionality. For the period 2025–2028, the Confederation has also allocated 250 million francs to supplement the basic funding.
For the first time, the report also examines the approximately 25 000 bus stops, which fall under the responsibility of the owners of the respective roads: Cantons, Cities and Municipalities. Fifty per cent can be used by passengers with reduced mobility; in some cases independently, in others with the assistance of staff. Forty-two per cent are inaccessible and require alternative measures, generally a shuttle service provided by the transport company to the nearest stop compliant with the LDis.
The report also records the difficulties that Cantons, Cities and Municipalities encounter in implementation: limited space and sloping terrain, conflicts with other land uses, complex procedures and delays caused by objections. DCPA, UCS and ACS support the authorities with documentation and knowledge transfer. This is the distinction that anyone using mezzi pubblici must bear in mind when reading the progress of the work. ## Two networks, two levels of accessibility
The comparison between the number of stations and the share of passengers should not be read as a single percentage. Railways and buses have different responsibilities and operating conditions, and the source distinguishes between independent use, staff assistance and replacement measures.
### Why the comparison matters
| Network | Status observed | Operational consequence | |---|---|---| | Rail | 1168 out of approximately 1800 can be used independently | 83 per cent of passengers can benefit from the works | | Buses | 50 per cent usable; 42 per cent inaccessible | Staff assistance or shuttle, as applicable |
The comparison shows that the national figure answers two different questions: how many stations and stops have been adapted, and how many passengers can benefit from the interventions. In rail transport, the initial modernization of the larger stations explains why the share of passengers is high compared with the total number of facilities. Planning through 2029, with another 193 adaptations, therefore measures the progress of the works and not a change that has already been implemented.
For buses, the 50 per cent figure brings together different situations. A stop may be used independently or require staff assistance; where it is inaccessible, the replacement measure indicated is generally a shuttle operated by the transport company to the nearest stop compliant with LDis. For people who use mezzi pubblici, the difference between independent use, assistance and shuttle is therefore a tangible part of interpreting the figure.
The responsible parties also differ. Railway companies are tasked with adapting railway stations and stops, while for bus stops the responsibility lies with the road owners, namely Cantons, Cities and Municipalities. The report notes that legal requirements have been incorporated into plans and processes, but limited space, sloping terrain, conflicts with other land uses, complex procedures and objections can slow down systematic and timely implementation.
Additional federal funding supports the 2025–2028 period, while the target of 87 per cent concerns rail planning by the end of 2029. These are therefore two time horizons that should not be confused when assessing the status of a national or cantonal network.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to use the report information
The most straightforward way to translate the national framework into a practical check is to proceed by stop type and accessibility level. The railway sector has a report and an implementation list; for buses, the report introduces for the first time a snapshot of the approximately 25,000 stops and indicates the responsible entities.
### Four practical steps
1. Identify the network. Determine whether the point to be used is a railway station/stop or a bus stop. This distinction determines which part of the report to consult and which responsibility to consider.
2. Check the railway. For railway stations and stops, the reference point is the 2026 Status Report with its attached list of DDA implementation status. This document allows users to read the framework of adjustments reported by the FOT without confusing the number of facilities with the passenger share.
3. Read the bus category. For a bus stop, responsibility lies with the road owner, namely the Canton, City, or Municipality. The data must be distinguished between autonomous use, staff assistance, and non-accessible stops. In the latter case, the generally provided replacement measure is the transport company's shuttle service to the nearest DDA-compliant stop.
4. Monitor delays and deadlines. When a railway project is delayed, the FOT requires transitional measures. The planning to keep an eye on extends until the end of 2029, while the Confederation's additional funding covers the 2025–2028 period. For the DDA, the original deadline for adjustments was the end of 2023, subject to the condition of proportionality of the intervention.
### The role of the authorities
Cantons, Cities, and Municipalities have integrated legal requirements into their plans and processes, but they must manage tight spaces, sloping terrain, conflicts with other land uses, complex procedures, and delays due to objections. The Swiss Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Public Works, Spatial Planning and Environment (BVPK), the Swiss Association of Cities (Städteverband), and the Swiss Association of Municipalities (Gemeindeverband) continue to support them with documentation and knowledge transfer. The report also plans to complement the quantitative data with best practice models aimed at the general public.

item.description: Switzerland has ranked first since 2011 in the WIPO ranking; Sweden and the United States follow, while China enters the top ten for the first time.

## In brief - Switzerland has ranked first since 2011 - Sweden and the United States complete the podium - China enters the top ten for the first time - The index uses 80 indicators and covers nearly 140 countries
## Key facts - Organization → WIPO - Edition → 18th - Indicators → 80 - Countries examined → nearly 140 - First place → Switzerland, since 2011 - Podium → Switzerland, Sweden, United States - New development → China among the top ten nations
### The Confederation's top spot GENEVA - Switzerland remains the world's most innovative country according to the ranking published each year by the World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO. The Confederation has held first place since 2011, a position confirmed in this 18th edition as well.
The podium is unchanged from last year: Sweden and the United States rank behind Switzerland. They are followed by South Korea, noted as having risen from sixth place, Singapore and the United Kingdom. The ranking continues with Finland, the Netherlands, Denmark and China. For China, this is the first time it has been among the top ten nations.
The result is not built on a single parameter. The index examines 80 indicators and scrutinizes nearly 140 countries. The elements considered include spending on research and development, venture capital transactions, high-tech exports and filings of applications for intellectual property rights.
### WIPO's interpretation WIPO Director Daren Tang links the fastest progress to countries that regard innovation as a driver of resilience, growth and competitiveness. In his assessment, innovation ecosystems must be supported and nourished by thoughtful policies, significant investment and cross-sector collaboration. This is the interpretive lens offered by the organization alongside the ranking.
The reference to continuity since 2011 distinguishes Switzerland's result from a simple one-year leap. At the same time, China's presence in the top ten signals a change in the composition of the leading group, while South Korea's rise from sixth place highlights movement at the top of the list.
The framework therefore makes it possible to read three separate pieces of information: Switzerland's position, the comparison with the podium and the breadth of the scope used to calculate the index. The source does not present a single project or a specific sector as the exclusive explanation for the top position. ## How to read the result in Switzerland
### An index, not a single parameter For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical point of the news is to understand that first place describes an overall position. The text does not identify it as the result of a single activity, a single company or a single sector. item.title: Lindt revises estimates: sales and prices decline
item.description: Lindt&Sprüngli cuts the 2026 organic growth forecast to 0-2 percent and is considering broader price reductions from January after the impact of cocoa and summer heat.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Organic growth in 2026 falls to 0-2 percent - Previous target was 4-6 percent - Lindt is considering broader reductions from January - The share price fell to 7960 francs
## Key facts - Organic growth in 2026 → 0-2 percent - Previous target → 4-6 percent - Broader reductions → starting in January - Morning share price → 7960 francs, -6,9 percent - Target from 2028 → annual organic growth of 6-8 percent
### The new scenario for Lindt In Zurich, Lindt&Sprüngli revised its revenue target downward for the second time. For 2026, the organic growth forecast is now between 0 and 2 percent, compared with the 4-6 percent indicated so far. At the beginning of the year, the company was still targeting 6-8 percent; that target was abandoned in March.
The announcement was made on Tuesday. The rationale combines two factors: price increases made necessary by rising cocoa prices and the heat wave that hit Europe during the summer. With high temperatures, consumers showed less interest in Lindor balls and pralines.
> “No one felt like entering a specialty chocolate shop at 37 degrees,” said CEO Adalbert Lechner.
The increases, according to the company’s explanation, could not be avoided. After an initial decline, cocoa prices rose again and, even after the price adjustments, weighed on the gross margin. Lindt also intends to act on costs, while job cuts are not under discussion.
The raw materials situation then eased somewhat. Lindt is therefore considering broader reductions starting in January, with the aim of obtaining a greater volume of orders for next Easter and the Christmas period. The company says it is confident about the coming months and 2027. For those living in Switzerland, the topic becomes part of the reading of costo della vita in Svizzera, without the communication turning the assessment into a generalized promise.
The group also maintains its goal of improving the EBIT margin by 20-40 basis points in 2026. For 2027, it expects renewed volume growth, supported by an adapted pricing strategy, greater investment in the brand and falling cocoa prices. Financial forecasts for 2027 will be published in the first quarter; from 2028, annual organic revenue growth of 6-8 percent remains confirmed, with an annual improvement in the EBIT margin of 20-40 basis points. ## What changes for those who buy and those who watch the stock market
### Prices, sales channels and confidence The first practical point for those living in Switzerland is to distinguish what has already been done from what Lindt is still considering. Some reductions have been applied in Switzerland and Germany; a broader measure is instead indicated as possible from January. This distinction avoids reading as a certain price cut a decision that the company still presents as under consideration.
| Step | Reported signal | Practical reading | | Reductions already made | Switzerland and Germany | Observe the price applied | | From January | Possible broader reductions | Check for any change | | Easter and Christmas | Goal of more orders | Monitor demand's response |
The place of purchase also factors into the reading of the data. Demand declined mainly in specialty stores, while the decline was less pronounced in supermarkets. For the Swiss market, the news therefore does not describe identical behavior in every channel: it links sales weakness to the heat, but signals a different impact between specialty stores and supermarkets.
For an individual or family's budget, the point is not to turn Lindt's forecast into savings that can already be quantified. The company speaks of somewhat more relaxed raw-material prices and a strategy aimed at recovering volumes; the benefit for buyers will depend on the concrete application of the reductions. The comparatore CHF/EUR can complement this reading when observing the two markets mentioned, without confusing the exchange rate with the pricing decision.
The stock market offers another perspective. In morning trading, Lindt participation certificates listed in the Midcap SMIM index fell by 6,9 percent to 7960 francs, below the 8000 threshold for the first time since 2021. Analysts fear a loss of confidence and question the group's forecasting ability; according to the prevailing view, Lindt would also have overestimated its own pricing power. For the reader, the decline in the share price measures the market's reaction to the revenue warning, not the price of a single package.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow developments
### Three practical steps 1. Separate the announcement from its application. When buying in Switzerland, check the price actually applied and do not treat the assessment of broader reductions as a discount that has already been generalized. The distinction is between reductions already implemented and measures that Lindt is still examining.
2. Use the occasions indicated by the company as checkpoints. The next Easter and the Christmas period are the windows during which Lindt wants to obtain a greater volume of orders. The reader can compare the price observed before these phases with the one available during purchases, without automatically attributing every change to heat or cocoa.
3. To follow the company, use two reference points: the publication, in the first quarter, of the financial forecasts for 2027 and the medium-term targets confirmed from 2028 onward. The comparison should be made between volume growth, pricing strategy, brand investments and EBIT margin, all indicators mentioned by the company.
This procedure keeps three levels separate: the price paid by the consumer, the volumes that Lindt wants to recover and the indicators included in the financial targets. The first is verified at the time of purchase; the others are read in the company's subsequent updates. In this way, a company target remains distinct from a result already achieved, and an analysts' assessment is not confused with the price charged in stores.
For personal budgeting, noting the actual changes makes it possible to link spending to one's own figures, without using estimates not indicated in the communication. To link spending to your monthly budget, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.description: Lindt expects revenue growth of 0%-2% (versus previous 4-6%), BP -8% in the morning, YTD performance -30%, -35% over 12 months, -24% over 5 years; headquarters in Kilchberg ZH, 15'500 employees.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Lindt expects turnover growth of between 0% and 2% - The previous estimate was 4-6% - The BP fell 8% in the morning - Seasonal orders are below expectations
## Key facts - Expected growth → 0%-2% of turnover - Previous estimate → 4-6% - Morning BP decline → 8% - Performance since the beginning of January → -30% - Performance over twelve months → -35% - Performance over five years → -24% - Headquarters → Kilchberg (ZH) - Workforce → 15'500 employees
### The revision of estimates
For the second time this year, Lindt & Sprüngli has revised its sales forecasts downward. The group now expects turnover growth of between 0% and 2%, compared with the 4-6% previously forecast. The revision comes after price increases initially caused by the surge in cocoa costs: consumer reaction was stronger than expected.
Keystone-ATS reports that price sensitivity and moderate consumer confidence have reduced order volumes, especially in the seasonal segment. The statement cites Germany, Switzerland and Austria.
> «Rather moderate consumer confidence and greater price sensitivity have resulted in order volumes below expectations, especially in the seasonal sector, particularly in Germany, Switzerland and Austria,» the statement reads.
Lindt also points to the wave of extreme heat that affected Europe during the summer: according to the company, it had a negative impact on revenues across the entire sector. Growth is instead described as solid in North America and Asia.
CEO Adalbert Lechner maintains that the decline in the price of cocoa from historic highs should gradually bring cost pressures back to normal. The company expects a recovery in demand and identifies 2027 as the year in which positive volume growth will be achieved, supported by pricing strategy, investments in brands, innovation and cost discipline.
On the stock market, the participation certificate, the BP, fell as much as 8% in the morning, while the market was generally oriented toward a fractional rise. The BP entitles holders to a dividend but not to voting rights and is the reference security for analysts. The indicated price is around 7970 francs; the security belongs to the SLI, which comprises the 30 most important stocks.
Performance is negative by 30% since the beginning of January, by 35% over twelve months and by 24% over five years. Lindt, backed by a 180-year tradition, has twelve of its own plants in Europe and the United States and 620 stores. In 2025 it generated turnover of 5,9 billion francs, up 8% thanks to strong price increases. ## How to read the signal in Switzerland
### Prices, volumes and markets
For those living in Switzerland, the most concrete indicator is the relationship between price and quantity sold. Lindt recorded revenue growth in 2025 thanks to strong price increases, but now reports orders below expectations for seasonal products. This alone does not prove that every price increase reduces demand, but it shows that price sensitivity has become an explicit variable in the group's estimates. Those tracking the cost of living in Switzerland can use this case as a company-specific indicator, without turning it into a general measure of prices.
The geography of demand changes the interpretation. Germany, Switzerland and Austria are the markets cited for the slowdown in seasonal orders; North America and Asia, by contrast, show solid growth. Extreme heat in Europe is a second factor identified by the company and concerns the revenues of the entire sector. The signal, therefore, is not uniform: it contains one component linked to prices and another connected to summer conditions.
| Signal | How to interpret it | |---|---| | Cocoa prices lower than historical highs | Cost pressures should gradually normalize | | Seasonal orders below expectations | Consumers' price sensitivity weighs on forecasts | | Growth in North America and Asia | Weakness is not described in all markets | | Target for 2027 | The company expects positive volume growth |
### The point for those watching the stock
For investors, the revision also matters for the credibility of forecasts. Jean-Philippe Bertschy, an analyst at Vontobel, warns that the second cut of the year weakens confidence in Lindt's ability to formulate accurate estimates. According to the comment, that ability had contributed to the stock's high valuation.
The question to follow is the one indicated by the analyst himself: does consumers' reaction to the increases reflect a structural problem of price elasticity or an isolated episode? In the first scenario, pricing power, long considered a strength of Lindt, remains under pressure. In the second, the normalization of cocoa costs and a recovery in demand may support the trajectory announced for 2027. These are interpretations anchored in the statements reported, not a new forecast.
The nature of the BP should also be kept distinct. The instrument recognizes the dividend, but not the vote; this is why it is the reference followed by analysts in the source. Its price movement should therefore be read together with the company's operating indications, not as a direct measure of households' chocolate purchases. To explore the impact of prices on the balance sheet, consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Procedure for the reader
### Five checks before drawing a conclusion
To use the press release as a reading tool, it is not enough to stop at the stock market movement. Follow these five steps, all based on the data provided by the company and the analyst's note.
1. Set the comparison. Put the new range 0%-2% next to the previous 4-6%. The first figure describes the current expectation for revenue growth; the second shows how much the forecast has been reduced.
2. Separate the factors. Keep distinct the spike in cocoa that had driven price increases, consumer sensitivity, seasonal orders and extreme heat in Europe. The source presents them as different elements of the revision.
3. Check the geographical area. Germany, Switzerland and Austria are associated with orders below expectations; North America and Asia with solid growth. This step avoids interpreting the slowdown as uniform across all markets.
4. Read the right security. The BP is entitled to the dividend but not to voting rights and is the reference for analysts. Therefore, compare its change in the morning with the periods since the beginning of January, twelve months and five years, without confusing the share price with sales volume.
5. Keep the two horizons separate. On the one hand, there is the CEO's expectation of positive volume growth in 2027; on the other, Vontobel's question about price elasticity, whether structural or isolated. Those looking at the scale of employment can pair the data on 15'500 employees and 620 stores with the search for aziende che assumono.
The result is a concrete reading guide: forecast, causes, geographies, financial instrument and time horizon remain separate. To link price movements to your monthly budget, use the calcolatore stipendio

item.title: Swiss workers use AI, but few see its benefits
item.description: 28% of Swiss workers use generative AI every day, but only 10% see improved work quality. Findings from PwC research.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 28% use generative AI every day in Switzerland - Only 10% see improved work quality - 14% feel more motivated or confident - Up to 9% believe that AI fosters skills and creativity
## Key facts - Research → «Hopes and Fears» 2026 by PwC - Swiss sample → 1000 employees - Period → between May and June - Daily use of generative AI → 28% - Global average of daily use → 22% - Clear improvement in work quality → 10% - Motivation or confidence thanks to AI → 14% - Skills and creativity fostered by AI → up to 9%
28% of Swiss workers use generative AI every day, compared with the global average of 22%. This figure comes from the 2026 edition of the «Hopes and Fears» research conducted by PwC, which describes a cautious relationship with artificial intelligence tools: in Switzerland, usage is higher than the international average, but perceived benefits remain limited.
Only 10% of respondents see a clear improvement in work quality. 14% say they feel more motivated or confident thanks to these tools. Up to 9% believe that AI fosters skills and creativity, while 22% say it helps them manage more complex tasks. The data show a gap between frequency of use and perceived benefit.
### Frequent use, less clear benefits
The figure should be read on two levels. On the one hand, the 28% indicates daily use by a portion of the Swiss sample. On the other, the percentages for quality, motivation, skills, creativity and complex tasks indicate that using the tool is not automatically associated with a better result. In the text, the proposed response involves support and targeted training, not daily use alone.
Teena Madhvani, an executive at PwC Svizzera, argues that job security and salary are not enough to attract and retain talent. Trust, flexibility, a strong corporate culture and transparent development opportunities are also needed. To make AI truly useful, she adds, support and targeted training are necessary.
For the 2026 edition, 1000 employees in Switzerland were interviewed between May and June. Globally, approximately 50'000 active workers in 48 countries participated in the research. The Swiss sample is therefore part of a broader survey, which places the national figure alongside the global average for the use of generative AI. ## Security today, future skills
The second section of the research shifts the focus from the use of AI to the perception of job stability. 66% of Swiss workers feel secure in their jobs for the next twelve months, but only 27% are optimistic about demand for their skills three years from now. The gap between the two time horizons indicates that immediate security does not coincide with confidence in the future marketability of one’s skills.
Another signal concerns trust. 21% trust their direct supervisor and 17% top management, while only 19% say they clearly know which skills will be required in the future. The perceived problem therefore concerns not only technology: it also includes the relationship with the hierarchy and the ability to orient oneself toward what will be needed.
### The signals that influence the choice of a job
| Indicator | Result | |---|---| | Negative culture as a reason to reject a job | 54% | | Opposition to greater control in the workplace | 40% |
The 54% share indicates that a culture perceived as negative can become a reason to reject a job. The 40% instead signals the limit placed on control in the workplace. Together, the two shares describe a demand for trust and room for autonomy.
For those reading annunci di lavoro, the practical implication is to look beyond security and salary: the source identifies trust, flexibility, a strong culture and transparent development as elements capable of attracting and retaining talent. The comparison with aziende che assumono can therefore start from these criteria, without reducing the choice to compensation alone.
The same message applies to the introduction of AI. Technology is perceived as useful when accompanied by support and targeted training. For organizations, the research therefore brings together two dimensions: making the tools usable and making the career path clear. For workers, this means evaluating tasks, future skills and the quality of the environment together.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From research to a personal assessment
The survey can become a personal assessment framework. It is not enough to ask only whether AI is being used: it is necessary to separate usage from the perceived effect and from the conditions that make it useful. The steps follow the themes indicated by the research.
### Four operational steps
1. **Map the tasks.** Distinguish the activities in which AI helps manage more complex tasks from those in which no clear improvement in quality can be seen. The question is not how often the tool is used, but what result is recognized.
2. Verify the support. Ask whether targeted support and training are available to make AI truly useful. The source identifies these two elements as necessary, so they should be considered together with everyday adoption.
3. Check the skills. Compare current activities with the skills that are expected to be required in the future. If the picture is unclear, the research shows that visibility into development remains an open issue.
4. Assess environment and autonomy. In a current job or a new one, examine company culture, flexibility, autonomy, trust, and level of control. These are the factors that the research places alongside security and salary.
For those considering new opportunities, this assessment prevents them from focusing on just one factor. For those already employed, it provides a framework for focusing the comparison on training, support, trust, and transparent development. The same framework makes it possible to distinguish frequent use of AI from use perceived as truly useful, without confusing adoption with results.
